data.title: Student discovers fungus predicted by Albert Hoffman
data.author: zafka
data.article_summary: 西弗吉尼亚大学（WVU）环境微生物学专业的学生Corinne Hazel发现了一种新的真菌物种，这种真菌可能用于治疗多种医疗疾病。她在研究牵牛花如何通过根部分泌麦角生物碱时，发现了一种名为*Periglandula clandestina*的新真菌，这种真菌能够产生与LSD类似的效果。她的发现是在与植物与土壤科学教授Daniel Panaccione合作下完成的，并得到了WVU Davis学院学生增强基金的资助。基因测序确认了这一新物种，其基因序列现已存入基因库。这种真菌能高效生产麦角生物碱，可能在未来药物开发中发挥重要作用。Hazel目前正在研究如何最佳地培养这种生长缓慢的真菌，并探索其他牵牛花物种是否也含有未被描述的真菌共生体。这一发现为医药和农业研究开辟了新的方向。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：与LSD、麦角生物碱、植物与真菌共生关系相关的科学发现及其影响

不同观点：
• [driggs] 认为霍夫曼（Albert Hoffman）在研究麦角酸酰二乙氨（LSA）时被指责样本污染，但后来由于植物与内共生真菌的关系被澄清而得到平反。霍夫曼的早期工作未考虑到植物内的隐秘真菌，但他的发现最终被证明是正确的。
• [Zaylan] 对新发现的共生关系表示赞赏，并推测自然界中可能还有许多未被发现的隐藏“化学家”——即在植物中悄悄进行复杂代谢过程的真菌。这引发了对日常植物中潜在未开发潜力的思考。
• [hollerith] 引用YouTube视频内容，质疑LSD可能引发创伤后应激障碍（PTSD），并提供视频链接以支持其观点，尽管未提供具体时间索引。
• [doormatt] 对研究中基因组测序的“重要性”提出质疑，认为既然测序是由外部公司完成的，那么其意义是否如文章所述那样重大。
• [homeonthemtn] 赞赏文章对迷幻化合物讨论时采取的成熟 tone（语气），表明对讨论此类敏感话题时应持谨慎态度。
• [gwbas1c] 对LSD被用于治疗抑郁症、创伤后应激障碍和成瘾等疾病的说法表示困惑，指出LSD属于附表1药物，理论上不应有合法用途，并提到与MDMA的合法实验情况不同。
• [randomNumber7] 强调LSA与LSD的不同，指出LSA可以从法律上获得，但其危险性可能高于LSD。
• [throwing_away] 询问是否可以获取克隆用于研究目的，显示出对研究资源的关注。
• [scythe] 指出，虽然麦角生物碱的合成衍生物（如麦角新碱）常用于治疗偏头痛、痴呆等疾病，但天然麦角本身难以培养，因此发现新的共生真菌具有重要意义。
• [zer00eyz] 对文章中LSD被用于治疗多种疾病的描述表示怀疑，认为这句话反映出文章在LSD问题上的语气存在问题，暗示LSD仍然是一个有争议的物质。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是LSD是否可以合法用于治疗目的，以及文章对LSD的描述是否准确。部分评论者对LSD的合法性和安全性提出质疑。
• 另一讨论点是基因组测序的“重要性”问题，尤其是当测序工作外包给其他公司时，其科学价值是否如文章所述那样重大。
• 评论中还涉及LSA与LSD的区别，以及LSA的合法性和潜在危险性。
• 最后，部分评论者表达了对植物与真菌共生关系的新发现及其潜在应用的兴趣和赞赏。

44243059.article_content:
WVU student discovers long-awaited mystery fungus sought by LSD’s inventor
Monday, June 02, 2025
Corinne Hazel, a WVU environmental microbiology major from Delaware, Ohio, has discovered a new species of fungus that may treat a variety of medical conditions.
(WVU Photo/Brian Persinger)
Download full-size
Making a discovery with the
potential for innovative applications in pharmaceutical development, a
West Virginia University
microbiology
student has found a long sought-after fungus that produces effects similar to the
semisynthetic drug LSD, which is used to treat conditions like depression,
post-traumatic stress disorder and addiction.
Corinne Hazel, of Delaware,
Ohio, an environmental microbiology major and
Goldwater
Scholar
, discovered the new species of fungus growing in morning
glory plants and named it Periglandula clandestina.
Hazel made the discovery
while working in the lab with
Daniel
Panaccione
, Davis-Michael Professor
of
Plant
and Soil Sciences
at the
WVU Davis College of Agriculture and
Natural Resources
. She
was studying how morning glories disperse protective chemicals called “ergot
alkaloids” through their roots when she saw evidence of a fungus.
“We had a ton of plants
lying around and they had these tiny little seed coats,” she said. “We noticed a
little bit of fuzz in the seed coat. That was our fungus.”
The researchers prepared a DNA sample
and sent it away for genome sequencing, funded by a
WVU Davis
College Student Enhancement Grant
obtained by Hazel. The sequencing confirmed
the discovery of a new species and the sequence is now deposited in a gene bank
with her name on it.
“Sequencing a genome is a significant
thing,” Panaccione said. “It’s amazing for a student.”
Morning glory plants live
in symbiosis with fungi that produce the same ergot alkaloids the Swiss chemist
Albert Hofmann modified when he invented LSD in the late 1930s.
Hofmann hypothesized that
a fungus in morning glories produced alkaloids similar to those in LSD, but the
species remained a mystery until Hazel and Panaccione’s discovery. They published their findings in
Mycologia
.
“Morning glories contain
high concentrations of similar lysergic acid derivatives that give them their
psychedelic activities,” Panaccione said. “This inspired Hofmann and others to
investigate morning glories for the presence of a hidden fungus related to the
ergot fungus that might be the source of these chemicals. They found very
similar chemicals, but they could never find the fungus itself.”
Ergot alkaloids are made
exclusively by fungi. In addition to morning glories, they’re often found
growing on grains like rye. They can be poisonous to humans and livestock and, when
used therapeutically, can have unwanted side effects. Still, some clinicians use
them to treat conditions like migraines, dementia, uterine hemorrhaging and
Parkinson’s disease.
Periglandula clandestina is highly
efficient at making ergot alkaloids in large quantities, a characteristic that may
play a role in future pharmaceuticals. The discovery of the fungus o
pens a host of potential research
avenues, Panaccione said.
“Many things are toxic. But if you
administer them in the right dosage or modify them, they can be useful
pharmaceuticals. By studying them, we may be able to figure out ways to bypass
the side effects. These are big issues for medicine and agriculture.”
The researchers dubbed the fungus “Periglandula
clandestina” for its ability to have eluded investigators for decades.
“I think that’s the perfect name,”
Panaccione said. “And I love that we did this project together. Corinne has a
ton of talent. It’s about students recognizing the opportunities, seizing them
and having the skill and the brain power to bring this work to fruition.”
Hazel is now studying the most
effective ways to culture the slow-growing fungus and is interested in whether other
morning glory species may also contain ergot alkaloids from a fungal symbiote
that has yet to be described.
“I’m lucky to have stumbled into this
opportunity,” she said. “People have been looking for this fungus for years,
and one day, I look in the right place, and there it is. I’m very proud of the
work that I’ve done at WVU.”
-WVU-

data.title: Simulink (Matlab) Copilot
data.author: kaamuli
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个名为Bloxi的项目，它是一个由帝国理工学院航空工程二年级学生开发的AI助手，能够将自然语言提示转换为可运行的Simulink控制系统模型，并进行实时调试。该项目利用OpenAI的API实现多模态功能，可以逐步生成和连接Simulink模块，并通过截图和LLM检查不一致之处。项目包含两个主要脚本和一个简单后端，用户只需输入自己的OpenAI API密钥即可使用。尽管最初只是个人项目，但随着MathWorks宣布开发类似工具，作者决定分享Bloxi，以供他人进一步开发和使用。项目遵循MIT许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Matlab和Simulink的应用及其工具的优缺点

不同观点：
• [kaamuli] 认为Matlab和Simulink在实际操作中存在效率问题，尤其是在构建和调试控制系统模型时，手动连接模块会浪费大量时间。为此，他开发了Bloxi，一个基于AI的助手，能够将自然语言提示转换为Simulink模型，并实时调试。他强调Bloxi的开发初衷是为了提高生产力，并分享了自己的开发经验和代码，希望其他人能进一步改进。

• [stochtastic] 则指出，虽然Matlab和Simulink在某些行业和学术领域已经不再流行，但它们在某些特定领域仍然具有无可比拟的优势。他提到对MathWorks产品的负面评价主要集中在许可证和商业模式上，而忽视了其技术优势。他鼓励不要被负面评价影响，认为应根据具体任务选择合适的工具。

补充讨论：
• [kaamuli] 提到了开发Bloxi过程中解决的具体技术问题，例如如何修复微分方程错误，以及如何通过脚本实现实时调试和模型构建。他还详细介绍了Bloxi的工作原理和使用方法，提供了视频演示和GitHub链接，方便他人使用和改进。

• 争议的焦点可能在于Matlab和Simulink的实际应用效率以及是否有更好的替代工具。虽然[kaamuli]指出了手动操作的低效，但[stochtastic]则强调了Matlab和Simulink在某些领域的不可替代性，反映了不同用户在使用体验上的差异。

• 另一个值得注意的点是，[kaamuli]提到MathWorks正在开发类似功能，这表明该工具的潜在价值和市场需求，同时也可能引发对竞争和创新的讨论。

• 最后，[kaamuli]的分享行为和开源精神也值得关注，他不仅提供了工具，还详细说明了使用方法和开发过程，促进了技术社区的合作与进步。

Before I start - Yes, I know the differential equation in the video is wrong. I’ve already fixed it by tweaking the prompt and the script so the inputs depend on what’s being asked. The original issue was that blocks like Sum were being pasted in without matching the right number of inputs and outputs.
I’m a 2nd-year aero-engineering student at Imperial College London, I enjoy problem solving (did BPhO - gold and UKMT Gold) I'm a full-stack dev (or atleast trying to be lol) who hacked together Bloxi, an AI copilot that sits on top of Simulink and turns plain-English prompts into working control-system models and can easily debug them in real time. I felt the pain myself this term, watching top-tier students burn hours wiring blocks instead of engineering. With today’s multimodal LLMs finally able to “see” diagrams, this is the first moment an assistant like Bloxi can exist and the fastest way to give millions of engineers the same productivity leap coders just got.I built this mainly to get comfortable with LLMs and “prompt-engineering,” and I think I’ve hit the point where I’m done tinkering—especially now that MathWorks have announced they’re working on their own version. So I figured I’d share what I’ve got in case anyone wants to take it further and also just to like give it out to the world innit.
How it works:
Two scripts + simple backend (3):
One builds the Simulink model.
The other handles the chat + simple UI.
Backend that glues together the OpenAI API and frontend
Drop in your own OpenAI API key and you’re off. I used it to debug and build a few uni-project models, and it’s been surprisingly handy.
At first it just spat out a finished Simulink file, but I wanted that ChatGPT “walk-through” vibe make it feel 'magical'. So I added a couple of for loops: one to drop in blocks step-by-step, and another to wire them up.
Since raw code isn’t visible in Simulink (to the best of my knowledge), within one of my scripts I had it walk through the simulink file and screenshot each stage leveraging the fact openAI's API is multimodal, pipe them through the LLM, and let it spot inconsistencies. Works better than I expected. Perhaps someone can do better or find a better way?
Youtube video of me using it is
https://youtu.be/TX0fviaFSyg
To use download & open scripts then just do openChatbox().

data.title: Last fifty years of integer linear programming: Recent practical advances (2024)
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary: 本文回顾了过去五十年混合整数线性规划（MILP）的进展，重点关注实际应用和近期计算性能的提升。MILP已成为运筹学的核心，现代求解器能高效解决十年前无法处理的问题，广泛应用于交通、物流、供应链、金融等领域。文章聚焦于分支定界法（branch-and-cut）、Dantzig-Wolfe分解和Benders分解三大方法，总结了关键研究成果，并指出MILP领域仍面临的挑战和未来研究方向。

主要讨论点：商业ILP求解器（如Gurobi）为何优于开源求解器，及其在实际应用中的表现和成本问题。

不同观点：
• [aquafox] 认为ILP问题由于其NP难性质，难以找到通用的高效解法，商业求解器通过大量针对特定子问题的启发式算法实现性能提升，而这些方法未进入公共领域。
• [dcminter] 通过自身经历说明算法和硬件的进步带来了巨大的性能提升，特别是在资源分配工具中，这种提升尤为明显，问题解决时间从长期运行缩短到几分钟。
• [tormeh] 提出实际应用中数值优化的实现可能因数据问题（如信任、数据质量）而失败，最终决策可能依赖于个人经验和直觉。
• [pradn] 引用研究数据，指出自1988年以来，LP求解器的速度提升了3300倍，结合硬件提升，整体性能提高了数百万倍，并提出在不同计算子领域中比较算法和硬件提升的必要性。
• [djoldman] 关注Gurobi的高昂价格，询问具体定价细节。
• [FabHK] 通过历史对比，说明自1990年代以来，求解LP问题的时间大幅缩短，现代MILP求解器的性能提升显著。
• [beret4breakfast] 认为目前基于ML/AI的方法在解决ILP等优化问题上效果不佳，实际应用中更高效的方法仍是运筹学（OR）方法，并分享了自己在调度优化中使用进化算法的经验。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了商业求解器Gurobi的高性能和昂贵价格，以及算法和硬件进步对求解速度的巨大影响。
• 实际应用中，数值优化的实现可能面临数据质量和信任问题，导致最终决策依赖于人工判断。
• 讨论中还涉及了ML/AI方法在ILP问题上的应用现状，目前看来这些方法尚不足以替代商业求解器。
• 历史对比和性能提升的数据为理解商业求解器的优势提供了量化支持。

Abstract
en
Mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) has become a cornerstone of operations research. This is driven by the enhanced efficiency of modern solvers, which can today find globally optimal solutions within seconds for problems that were out of reach a decade ago. The versatility of these solvers allowed successful applications in many areas, such as transportation, logistics, supply chain management, revenue management, finance, telecommunications, and manufacturing. Despite the impressive success already obtained, many challenges remain, and MILP is still a very active field.
This article provides an overview of the most significant results achieved in advancing the MILP solution methods. Given the immense literature on this topic, we made deliberate choices to focus on computational aspects and recent practical performance improvements, emphasizing research that reports computational experiments. We organize our survey into three main parts, dedicated to branch-and-cut methods, Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition, and Benders decomposition. The paper concludes by highlighting ongoing challenges and future opportunities in MILP research.

data.title: Solar Orbiter gets world-first views of the Sun's poles
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary:
欧洲航天局（ESA）的太阳轨道器（Solar Orbiter）通过倾斜轨道，首次从黄道平面之外拍摄到太阳两极的图像。以往的太阳图像都来自太阳赤道区域，而太阳轨道器的新视角将帮助科学家更好地理解太阳的磁场、太阳活动周期及空间天气。2025年3月，太阳轨道器在距离太阳赤道17度的角度观测到南极，并计划未来进一步倾斜轨道以获得更佳视角。

太阳轨道器的科学仪器，包括偏振与日震成像仪（PHI）、极紫外成像仪（EUI）和日冕环境光谱成像仪（SPICE），提供了多角度的太阳观测数据。初步发现显示，太阳南极的磁场在太阳活动高峰期非常混乱，南北极磁场混合存在。这为了解太阳磁场翻转及11年活动周期提供了新线索。太阳轨道器的独特观测将开启太阳科学的新时代。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人类首次近距离观察太阳极区的意义及相关技术细节

不同观点：
• [ahmedfromtunis] 认为，尽管人类对太阳的了解似乎很全面，但实际上非常有限，这次对太阳极区的观察提醒了我们这一点。他对科学探索工作表示支持和鼓励。
• [lostlogin] 对新闻中使用的“World First”表述提出质疑，认为“First Ever”可能更为合适。
• [superkuh] 指出，目前的观测只是稍微倾斜的角度，而非完全俯瞰极区。原本的计划是让探测器进入一个高倾角轨道，但因成本问题改为更便宜的方案，仅能提供接近黄道平面的观测。尽管如此，他认为这次任务仍然很酷。
• [sandworm101] 以幽默的方式表达了对未发现预期现象（如六边形结构）的失望，可能是因为一个旧赌约。
• [colordrops] 认为这次观测虽然看似微小，但实际上是人类历史上首次看到太阳极区，意义重大，令人惊叹。
• [wtcactus] 纠正其他评论者，指出1994-1995年Ulysses探测器已经进行过太阳极区探测，认为当前新闻报道中的声明不准确。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否真的是人类首次观测太阳极区。 [wtcactus] 提供了Ulysses探测器的例子，认为那才是首次。
• [superkuh] 提供了关于任务规划和预算削减的背景信息，指出原本有更雄心勃勃的计划，但因成本问题改为当前方案。
• 部分评论者如[ahmedfromtunis]和[colordrops]表达了对科学探索的积极态度和敬畏之情，而[lostlogin]和[sandworm101]则更多关注表述和幽默效果。

ESA

Solar Orbiter
Thanks to its
newly tilted orbit
around the Sun, the European Space Agency-led
Solar Orbiter
spacecraft is the first to image the Sun’s poles from outside the ecliptic plane. Solar Orbiter’s unique viewing angle will change our understanding of the Sun’s magnetic field, the
solar cycle
and the workings of space weather.
Solar Orbiter zooms into the Sun’s south pole
Access the video
Any image you have ever seen of the Sun was taken from around the Sun’s equator. This is because Earth, the other planets, and all other operational spacecraft orbit the Sun within a flat disc around the Sun called the ecliptic plane. By tilting its orbit out of this plane, Solar Orbiter reveals the Sun from a whole new angle.
The video above compares Solar Orbiter’s view (in yellow) with the one from Earth (grey), on 23 March 2025. At the time, Solar Orbiter was viewing the Sun from an angle of 17° below the solar equator, enough to directly see the Sun’s south pole. Over the coming years, the spacecraft will
tilt its orbit even further
, so the best views are yet to come.
“Today we reveal humankind’s first-ever views of the Sun’s pole,” says Prof. Carole Mundell, ESA's Director of Science. “The Sun is our nearest star, giver of life and potential disruptor of modern space and ground power systems, so it is imperative that we understand how it works and learn to predict its behaviour. These new unique views from our Solar Orbiter mission are the beginning of a new era of solar science.”
All eyes on the Sun’s south pole
Solar Orbiter's world-first views of the Sun's south pole
The collage above shows the Sun’s south pole as recorded on 16–17 March 2025, when Solar Orbiter was viewing the Sun from an angle of 15° below the solar equator. This was the mission’s first high-angle observation campaign, a few days before reaching its current maximum viewing angle of 17°.
The images shown above were taken by three of
Solar Orbiter’s scientific instruments
: the Polarimetric and Helioseismic Imager (PHI), the Extreme Ultraviolet Imager (EUI), and the Spectral Imaging of the Coronal Environment (SPICE) instrument. Click on the image to zoom in and see video versions of the data.
“We didn’t know what exactly to expect from these first observations – the Sun’s poles are literally
terra incognita
,” says Prof. Sami Solanki, who leads the PHI instrument team from the Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research (MPS) in Germany.
The instruments each observe the Sun in a different way. PHI images the Sun in visible light (top left) and maps the Sun’s surface magnetic field (top centre). EUI images the Sun in ultraviolet light (top right), revealing the million-degree charged gas in the Sun’s outer atmosphere, the corona. The SPICE instrument (bottom row) captures light coming from different temperatures of charged gas above the Sun’s surface, thereby revealing different layers of the Sun's atmosphere.
By comparing and analysing the complementary observations made by these three imaging instruments, we can learn about how material moves in the Sun’s outer layers. This may reveal unexpected patterns, such as polar vortices (swirling gas) similar to those seen around the poles of
Venus
and
Saturn
.
These groundbreaking new observations are also key to understanding the Sun’s magnetic field and why it flips roughly every 11 years, coinciding with a peak in solar activity. Current models and predictions of the
11-year solar cycle
fall short of being able to predict exactly when and how powerfully the Sun will reach its most active state.
PHI sees mixed-up magnetism at the Sun's south pole
Messy magnetism at solar maximum
One of the first scientific findings from Solar Orbiter’s polar observations is the discovery that at the south pole, the Sun’s magnetic field is currently a mess. While a normal magnet has a clear north and south pole, the PHI instrument’s magnetic field measurements show that both north and south polarity magnetic fields are present at the Sun’s south pole.
This happens only for a short time during each solar cycle, at solar maximum,
when the Sun’s magnetic field flips and is at its most active
. After the field flip, a single polarity should slowly build up and take over at the Sun’s poles. In 5–6 years from now, the Sun will reach its next solar minimum, during which its magnetic field is at its most orderly and the Sun displays its lowest levels of activity.
“How exactly this build-up occurs is still not fully understood, so Solar Orbiter has reached high latitudes at just the right time to follow the whole process from its unique and advantageous perspective,” notes Sami.
PHI's pole-to-pole view of the Sun's magnetic field
PHI’s view of the full Sun’s magnetic field puts these measurements in context. The darker the colour (red/blue), the stronger the magnetic field is along the line of sight from Solar Orbiter to the Sun.

data.title: How to Build Conscious Machines
data.author: hardmaru
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：意识的本质及其在人工智能和哲学中的解释

不同观点：
• [AIorNot] 认为意识是一种主观体验，无法通过物理理论完全解释。即使我们能够关联神经活动和思想，但神经活动本身并不是思想。该评论质疑任何物理意识理论能否真正解释意识现象。
• [talkingtab] 关注实际应用，特别是如何构建有意识的机器。该评论质疑文章是否提供了可操作的指导，并指出AI中的“知识”和“能力”之间的区别。同时，提出复杂适应系统（CAS）可能具有意识，例如RIP路由协议。
• [trod1234] 反对创造有意识的机器，认为这是浪费资源。他们认为，人类已经有能力通过生育孩子来创造有意识的生命，而创造其他有意识的存在没有实际意义，并可能导致道德问题。
• [esafak] 简要介绍了论文中的五阶段意识层次，并指出论文声称解决了意识的难题，但未详细说明如何评估某个有机体属于哪个阶段。该评论还提到了IIT（整合信息理论）作为可能的评估方法。
• [Avicebron] 对文章中提到的多种理论和解释表示怀疑，认为其没有充分论证。
• [qgin] 认为我们只能知道自己有意识，但无法知道他人是否有意识。我们假设他人有意识是为了获得同样的礼貌对待。
• [disambiguation] 质疑论文中对“基质依赖”的处理，认为作者没有充分解释或证明为何可以忽略基质独立性。该评论指出，生物智能的进展都依赖于相同的基质，因此假设基质独立性并不合理。
• [gcanyon] 提出是否需要在AI中实现意识以达到特定目标的问题。该评论认为，某些任务可能不需要意识，而意识可能是高度智能系统的副产品。
• [catigula] 认为当前关于意识的理论都不完美，推荐了泛心论和Russellian monism作为可能的理论方向。该评论指出，意识问题被称为“难题”是有原因的。
• [canadiantim] 质疑论文中对“感受性（qualia）”的处理，认为论文假设感受性可以被进一步分解，但没有提供证据。该评论认为，感受性是不可还原的基本元素。
• [briian] 提出通过深入理解人脑来改进AI系统的可能性，指出人工神经网络和大型语言模型都受到人脑结构的启发。
• [nativeit] 以幽默的方式表达了对不同繁殖选择方式的尊重。
• [m3kw9] 质疑如何定义和测试意识。
• [PunchTornado] 认为文章没有提出新的观点，许多内容在Chalmers和Dennett等人的工作中已经被更深入地讨论过。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于意识是否可以被物理理论解释，以及是否应该或能够创造有意识的机器。

data.title: Meta-analysis of three different notions of software complexity
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary:
这篇文章总结了三种软件复杂性的概念：

1. **Rich Hickey的复杂性概念**：Hickey认为简单性意味着“单一性”——一个事物应具有“一个折叠/辫子、一个角色、一个任务、一个概念、一个维度”，不应混杂其他元素。他区分了“简单”和“容易”，前者是客观的，而后者是主观的，依赖于个人的判断。Hickey强调，简单性有助于易于理解、易于更改、调试和灵活性。他还对比了“交织”（complect）和“组合”（compose），主张避免交织以减少复杂性。

2. **John Ousterhout的复杂性概念**：Ousterhout认为复杂性是任何让系统难以理解和修改的结构，并强调“显而易见性”是系统设计的重要目标。显而易见性意味着开发者能快速理解代码并做出正确修改，减少认知负担。复杂性主要来源于依赖性和模糊性，依赖性无法完全消除，但应尽量减少。

3. **Zach Tellman的复杂性概念**：文章未详细展开，但强调复杂性常源于系统各部分的相互作用和时间维度。

这三种观点都旨在通过减少交织和依赖，使软件更易于理解和维护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件复杂性的定义与衡量

不同观点：
• [perrygeo] 支持Tellman的观点，认为简单性是软件与人类期望之间的契合，具有主观性。他认为简单性与软件在人脑中形成的预测模型相关，而不是单纯的技术指标如数量或交织度。这种观点强调主观体验和人对系统的理解。
• [burakemir] 认为在特定场景（如处理紧急系统故障）中，Tellman的主观视角可能不适用。在这种情况下，客观的改进和减少系统理解难度更为重要。他指出，虽然主观视角有其价值，但在某些实际操作情境中，更需要客观的标准。
• [_benton] 更倾向于Ousterhout的观点，认为其更为具体。同时指出“依赖”这一术语在不同情境下可能具有不同含义，并提出通过假设的数量来衡量复杂性。
• [amelius] 提到正交性（orthogonality）在讨论中被忽略，暗示这是另一种衡量软件复杂性的重要角度。
• [readthenotes1] 引用研究文章，指出代码行数（LOC）与多种复杂性度量高度相关，认为简单关注代码行数也能接近复杂性度量的结果。
• [adityaathalye] 用火箭方程比喻软件复杂性，强调复杂性是动态多维的，并通过时间和空间维度来解释。他提到行为对复杂性的影响，并指出即使复杂的静态系统也可能比动态系统更简单。
• [0xbadcafebee] 提出软件讨论可以分为哲学、科学和功能三个层次。哲学层次关注理解和解释，科学层次追求客观和共识，而功能层次则是日常开发实践。他认为大多数开发者主要关注功能层次，而非哲学或科学讨论。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于简单性/复杂性是主观的还是客观的。部分评论者（如perrygeo和burakemir）对主观和客观视角进行了对比，并讨论了不同情境下的适用性。
• 一些评论者（如_benton和amelius）提到了术语定义和未被讨论的概念（如正交性），扩展了讨论的范围。
• 技术性度量（如LOC和 McCabe 循环复杂度）在复杂性讨论中的角色也被提及，强调了简单度量指标的实际应用价值。
• 0xbadcafebee的评论为讨论提供了一个框架，帮助理解不同层次的软件讨论如何相互作用和区别。

44274696.article_content:
A meta-analysis of three different notions of software complexity
I want to discuss three different notions of software complexity:
Rich Hickey’s notion of complexity, as explained in his talk
Simple Made Easy
.
John Ousterhout’s notion of complexity, as explained in his book
A Philosophy of Software Design
.
Zach Tellman’s notion of complexity, as explained in his newsletter
Explaining Software Design
.
I’ve picked these three because I’ve found them to be at least somewhat coherent,
and the former two to be (relatively) well-known;
this blog post is not meant to be exhaustive
of all different definitions of complexity that have been
offered over the years.
The definitions summarized
(Formatting note: exact quotes are taken from the above-mentioned work.)
Hickey complexity
Hickey defines something as being simple as having some kind of oneness - he uses the phrases “one fold/braid, one role, one task, one concept, one dimension.” Hickey states, “When you’re looking for something simple, you want to see it have focus in these areas. You don’t want to see it combining things.”
Hickey contrasts ‘easy’ with ‘simple’. For ‘easy’, the central idea is proximity – in terms of access (e.g. already having something be installed, being able to easily install something), in terms of existing skills and capabilities, and so on. Hickey points out that ‘easy’ is subjective, because it is relative to the person making the judgement.
As one example here, Hickey states that the parentheses in Clojure are hard (i.e. the opposite of easy) but simple, and that
it is users’ responsibility
to fix this.
On the other hand, Hickey states that this notion of simplicity is objective, “we can probably go and look and see, I don’t see any connections, I don’t see where this twists with something else.”
Hickey stresses the difference between simplicity and low cardinality (“But not: One instance, one operation.”). He points out that the important thing is “lack of interleaving, not cardinality.”
Hickey sums up his argument against complexity as follows:
“We can only hope to make reliable those things we can understand”
“We can only consider a few things at a time”
“Intertwined things must be considered together”
“Complexity undermines understanding”
According to Hickey, simplicity has the following benefits:
Ease of understanding
Ease of change
Easier debugging
Flexibility
In terms of examples, Hickey has a few slides in his presentation
with some tables. The table below is a more condensed representation
of Hickey’s tables:
I may have misunderstood something; corrections welcome.
Complexity
Complects
Simpler alternative
State, objects
Everything that touches it
Values
Objects
State, identity, value
Values
Methods
Function and state, namespaces
Functions, namespaces
Variables
Value, time
Managed refs
Inheritance
Types
Polymorphism a la carte
Switch/matching
Multiple who/what pairs
Polymorphism a la carte
Syntax
Meaning, order
Data
Imperative loops, fold
what/how
Set functions
Actors
what/who
Queues
Variables
Value, time
Values
ORM
OMG
Declarative data manipulation
Conditionals
Why, rest of program
Rules
As one example, Hickey points out that “having state in your program is never simple”
and “The only time you can really get rid of it,
is it you present a functional interface on the outside,
a true functional interface, same input, same output.”
Hickey contrasts the words “complect” (to intertwine, interleave, braid)
and “compose” (to place together).
Ousterhout complexity
According to Ousterhout, “Complexity is anything related to the structure
of a software system that makes it hard to understand
and modify the system.” (Sec 2.1)
A closely related aspect is obviousness;
a system is considered to be obvious if
“a developer can quickly understand how the existing code works
and what is required to make a change”
and they “can make a quick guess about what to do,
without thinking very hard,
and yet be confident that the guess is correct” (Sec 2.2)
as well as “their first guesses about the behavior or
meaning of the code will be correct” (Ch. 18)
Ousterhout points out that obviousness is one
of the most important goals for system design;
and that obviousness is the opposite of high cognitive load
and unknown unknowns (see definitions below).
In Chapter 18, Ousterhout emphasizes the obviousness
is “in the mind of the reader” and that
“If someone reading your code says it’s not obvious,
then it’s not obvious, no matter how clear it may seem to you.”
“Complexity is caused by two things: dependencies and obscurity” (Sec 2.3) which are defined as:
“A dependency exists when a given piece of code cannot be understood and modified in isolation; the code relates in some way to other code, and the other code must be considered and/or modified if the given code is changed”.

data.title: How multiplication is defined in Peano arithmetic
data.author: nill0
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了递归原则在数学中的重要性和其常被误解的现象，特别是在自然数的加法和乘法定义中的应用。作者指出，尽管递归在现代数学中无处不在，但很多人，包括一些学生和维基百科的解释，常常未能正确理解和阐明这一概念。文章特别强调，乘法并不是简单重复的加法，这种错误的表述在基础数学教育中尤为常见。作者认为，即使在教学中为了简化而省略一些细节，也不应向学生传达错误的信息。递归原则是一个关键的存在性断言，用于从后继函数构造加法，并从加法定义乘法，缺乏这个原则就无法正确定义这些运算。文章最后呼吁对递归原则的重视，并解释其在数学中的必要性和应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“乘法作为重复加法”与递归定义的争议，以及在不同数学背景下递归和加法的定义与应用。

不同观点：
• [grogers] 认为在编程中，迭代和递归在功能上是等价的，可以相互转换。因此，他不理解为什么在数学中“乘法作为重复加法”的定义会被批评，觉得这种定义没有问题。
• [nrds] 指出文章中关于递归与无穷相关的论述是基于集合论基础的，但这不是唯一的视角。在如Coq、Lean和Agda等证明助手的类型理论中，递归与有限的结构密切相关，并且在这些背景下，递归是一个定义明确的计算过程。
• [BoiledCabbage] 对比了两种不同的加法递归定义，提出了关于两种定义是否存在显著差异的问题。第一种定义是逐步减少b并加到总和上，第二种定义则是将b减少的部分加到a上。
• [im3w1l] 探讨了在没有递归公理的情况下，所谓的“超自然数”的可能性。他描述了在没有递归公理时，可能存在的不同数集结构（如N的副本、Z的副本等），并讨论了在这种情况下的加法定义及其潜在结果。他认为这种定义可能会产生一致但不太有趣或有用的扩展。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是递归定义在不同数学背景下的应用和解释。一些人认为递归在某些背景下是有限且明确的，而文章中提到的与无穷相关的论述并不必要。
• 关于加法定义的具体形式，BoiledCabbage提出的两种定义方式引起了对其实际差异的讨论。
• im3w1l的扩展讨论展示了在没有递归公理的情况下，加法定义可以有不同的一致性扩展，这为理解递归和加法提供了新的视角。

44274854.article_content:
A familiar joke in mathematical logic (the field I worked in for the first twenty years of my career) is the following hypothetical entry in a mathematical dictionary:
Recursion
See “Recursion”.
Though recursion is ubiquitous in modern mathematics, even at the most basic level of the analysis of the arithmetic of natural numbers, it is a subtle concept, easily misunderstood. At its heart is the always problematic step from the finite to the infinite.  Having taught set theory and the foundations of mathematics for many years at various universities, I long ago learned that many students never do fully grasp it.
Many sources gloss over it. For example, the
Wikipedia entry
for the Peano Axioms for the natural numbers, which on the whole is pretty good, refers to “
recursion
”
to justify its definitions of addition and multiplication on the natural numbers, but the Wikipedia page it links to punts when it comes to properly explaining the all important Recursion Principle, let alone proving it (the set-theoretic Recursion Theorem), giving a sketch proof of uniqueness (easy) but not the crucial existence part (which many people find tricky). [My comments refer to the pages when I accessed them on October 31, 2011.]
The widespread lack of appreciation for the Recursion Principle (it’s a principle you
use
when you are developing Peano arithmetic, a theorem you
prove
when you are doing set theory) lay behind many of the erroneous comments I received in response to my series of articles on multiplication not being repeated addition (not even on the natural numbers). Those articles appeared on
MAA Online
in
June 2008
,
July-August 2008
,
September 2008
, and
January 2011
.
If you really understand the Recursion Principle, which is what is
required
in order to construct addition from the successor function and to define multiplication from addition, then you will know that addition is
not
repeated successor (though oddly, no one ever claimed that to be the case) and multiplication is
not
repeated addition.
ASIDE:
This is not an article about mathematics education. How teachers introduce addition and multiplication is another issue. I am not, repeat not, suggesting we teach recursion in the K-12 system. My complaint throughout that previous exchange was that, whatever and however we teach in our schools, we should not be stating things that are flat wrong. In this column I want to explain the recursion principle, its importance, its power, its need in mathematics, and how it is used, so you too will know why it is flat wrong to tell kids that multiplication is repeated addition. Remember, even if you don’t see the purpose of all the mathematical navel-inspection that led to the formulation of the principle, some of the students in your class may well find themselves wanting or needing to understand it in a few years time. While it is often pedagogically wise to say less than the whole truth, we should not lie to our students.
Okay, I’m back off my pulpit. The Recursion Principle is a rabbit-out-of-the-hat existence assertion. When used to construct addition from the successor function in Peano arithmetic, it tells you that there is a function from NxN to N that, lo-and-behold, can in any specific instance (i.e., for any pair of specific natural number arguments) be calculated by repeatedly applying the successor function a fixed number of times. Likewise, when the recursion principle is used to construct multiplication from addition in Peano arithmetic, it tells you that there is a function from NxN to N that, again wonder-of-wonders, can in any specific instance (i.e., for any pair of specific natural number arguments) be calculated by repeatedly adding a fixed number of times.

44274854.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“乘法作为重复加法”与递归定义的争议，以及在不同数学背景下递归和加法的定义与应用。

不同观点：
• [grogers] 认为在编程中，迭代和递归在功能上是等价的，可以相互转换。因此，他不理解为什么在数学中“乘法作为重复加法”的定义会被批评，觉得这种定义没有问题。
• [nrds] 指出文章中关于递归与无穷相关的论述是基于集合论基础的，但这不是唯一的视角。在如Coq、Lean和Agda等证明助手的类型理论中，递归与有限的结构密切相关，并且在这些背景下，递归是一个定义明确的计算过程。
• [BoiledCabbage] 对比了两种不同的加法递归定义，提出了关于两种定义是否存在显著差异的问题。第一种定义是逐步减少b并加到总和上，第二种定义则是将b减少的部分加到a上。
• [im3w1l] 探讨了在没有递归公理的情况下，所谓的“超自然数”的可能性。他描述了在没有递归公理时，可能存在的不同数集结构（如N的副本、Z的副本等），并讨论了在这种情况下的加法定义及其潜在结果。他认为这种定义可能会产生一致但不太有趣或有用的扩展。

• 争议的焦点之一是递归定义在不同数学背景下的应用和解释。一些人认为递归在某些背景下是有限且明确的，而文章中提到的与无穷相关的论述并不必要。
• 关于加法定义的具体形式，BoiledCabbage提出的两种定义方式引起了对其实际差异的讨论。
• im3w1l的扩展讨论展示了在没有递归公理的情况下，加法定义可以有不同的一致性扩展，这为理解递归和加法提供了新的视角。

data.article_summary: 本文对比了1970年代的超级计算机Cray 1与现代的Raspberry Pi 5（RPi5）的性能和价格。Cray 1在当时是顶尖的超级计算机，重达5吨，功耗115KW，运算速度为160MFLOPS，售价相当于今天的4000万美元，仅售出约100台，主要用于科学计算。相比之下，RPi5重量仅50克，功耗12W，运算速度达30GFLOPS，售价仅120美元。作者感叹计算机技术在过去几十年里的飞速发展，并展望未来人工智能和硬件的进一步突破。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：现代计算设备（如Raspberry Pi、GPU）与历史上的超级计算机（如Cray-1）的性能对比，以及如果将现代技术带回过去可能产生的影响。

不同观点：
• **qingcharles**：通过将现代高性能PC的性能与TOP500超级计算机的历史数据对比，推测其在1993年可以成为世界上最强大的超级计算机，并在1980年超越当时全球所有计算机的综合性能。
• **Animats**：提到2020年有人用FPGA构建了一个兼容Cray-1指令集的小型模型，强调Cray-1的简单架构和使用离散组件构建的特点。
• **dahart**：通过其前老板分享的故事，讲述Turner Whitted在1980年关于实时光线追踪计算需求的预测。对比现代GPU性能，指出当前消费级GPU的性能已经超越了当时每像素一台Cray的预测。
• **_tom_**：提到Raspberry Pi加上不到100美元的加速卡可以达到30 TFLOPs，显示出价格性能比的巨大提升。
• **smcameron**：分享了一个3D打印的Cray YMP机箱用于Raspberry Pi的项目链接，更多是趣味性而非技术讨论。
• **ziofill**：表达了一种幻想，即如果将现代技术带回历史展示给过去的科学家或名人，可能会产生极大的震撼效果。
• **delichon**：假设在1977年展示Raspberry Pi，可能会让人难以置信，并联想到科幻作品中的场景，如《星际迷航》中的Scotty与鼠标对话。
• **_fat_santa**：提出如果通过时间机器将Raspberry Pi 5提供给过去的科学家使用，可能会引发疯狂的实验，并联想到当年Cray-1的稀缺性和科学家的需求。
• **dale_huevo**：对比Cray-1的160 MFLOPS与Raspberry Pi的30 GFLOPS，调侃现代计算能力被用于处理网页相关的任务。
• **benob**：认为应该将Cray-1与现代的Raspberry Pi Pico 2进行对比，因为它们的规格更接近。
• **dgacmu**：指出Raspberry Pi 5的对比可能过于高配，建议使用Raspberry Pi Zero 2（成本约15美元）来与Cray-1进行更合理的比较，同时提到内存容量的差异。
• **bombcar**：质疑当年Cray-1所解决的问题是否仍在使用现代硬件进行解决，以及这些问题是否已经全部解决。
• **hoppp**：提到Cray-1的外观 futuristic，像《星际迷航》中的设备，并联想到垃圾桶Mac的设计灵感可能来源于此。
• **jwr**：质疑现代计算能力的提升是否带来了比过去超级计算机数千倍更好的实际问题解决效果，认为虽然计算能力提升巨大，但实际成果的提升并没有那么显著。

• 讨论中反复出现的一个主题是现代计算设备在性能上的巨大飞跃以及其相对低廉的成本，与历史上的超级计算机形成鲜明对比。
• 另一个值得注意的点是对过去超级计算机使用场景的怀旧与现代计算能力的实际应用效果之间的对比和思考。
• 多个评论提到了将现代技术带回过去可能引发的震撼和影响，反映出对技术进步速度的惊叹。

Cray versus Raspberry Pi
11 June 2025
I fondly recall the era when the pinnacle of supercomputing was the Cray 1.
Even the shape of this computer was massively different to anything that came before
and it was so futuristic that it could have come straight from a scifi movie.
While almost all other computers of the 1970s were just a collection of huge rectangular
cabinets with blinky lights and perhaps a few tape drives, the Cray 1 looked more like
a piece of space-age furniture and seemed very small for what it was.
Never the less, the Cray was a pretty hefty bit of kit, weighing in at over 5 tonnes
(most of that being the cooling system) and consuming a staggering 115KW of electricity
when its 64-bit processor was chugging along at 80MHz and interrogating the 8MB of
memory it was attached to.
Those numbers, and the 160MFLOPS of raw performance may have been mind-blowing "back in the
day" but when you compare them to what we can buy today you'll likely be even more shocked.
The Cray 1 cost an astounding US$8 million in 1977 which, if you adjust for inflation,
is equal to more than US$40 million in today's dollars.
Suffice to say that at that price, only around 100 or so systems were ever sold and they
tended to be used for very specific scientific applications rather than as a general
purpose computer.
Let's jump forward about half a century to the present day and compare what was once the
world's fastest computer to something far more modest -- by today's standards.
The RPi5 is much smaller and lighter than the Cray 1, by many orders of magnitude. In
fact we're talking just 50g versus 10 tonnes.
The RPi5 uses far less power at around 12W versus the 115KW of the Cray.
But what about performance?  Can this tiny single-board computer match the awesome power
of what was once the fastest computer on the planet?
Well, as I mentioned earlier, the Cray had about 160MFLOPS of raw processing power; the Pi
has... up to 30GFLOPS.  Yes... that's *giga*FLOPS.  This makes it almost 200 times
faster than the Cray.
So how does the price compare then?
Well that Cray was US$40m in today's currency and an RPi5 will run you just US$120.
You can crunch your own numbers to calculate interesting things like the "bang per buck"
ratio of these two machines but it's very, very apparent through this comparison,
just how rapidly our computer technology has advanced over recent decades.
As someone who spent countless hours tinkering with early 8-bit microprocessors back
in the 1970s (when the Cray was king), it still astonishes me just how much raw processing
power, memory and storage we now consider to be "average".
That we can fit a terabyte onto a microSD card smaller than your thumbnail also boggles my mind --
especially when I remember all those years ago that a regular 16 pin DIP integrated circuit was
doing well to store
just a single Kbyte of data
.
I find it hard to believe that this rate of progress will continue unchecked for the next 50 years --
but then again if you'd showed me an RPi5 back in 1977 I would have said "nah, impossible" so
who knows?
If AI systems continue to improve at the current rate and we combine that with improvements in
hardware that are measured in orders of magnitude every 15 years or so then it stands to reason
that we'll get that "super-intelligent GAI" system any day now.
Once that happens I wonder if we'll be relegated to the role of "curious pets" by that
system?
Carpe Diem folks!

data.title: On the Usability of Editable Software
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了软件可编辑性的重要性，提出了与当前追求“可重用代码”不同的观点，主张“可再编辑代码”。作者以Knuth的观点为例，指出可以让用户根据自己需求修改代码，而不是在单一版本中包含所有可能的功能。这种方法可以使软件更小、更简单，因为只需提供核心功能，而非满足所有用户需求。目前软件开发常忽视用户修改的需求，导致软件难以更改，并形成恶性循环。作者建议设计时考虑用户可能进行的修改，从而简化软件，并减少因功能增加带来的复杂性。此外，插件和扩展虽然提供一定灵活性，但也带来维护和兼容性问题。最终，文章呼吁重新思考软件设计，使其更易于修改和定制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户是否会主动修改软件以满足个人需求，以及这种做法的可行性和优缺点。

不同观点：
• vivzkestrel认为大多数用户不会主动修改软件来满足自己的需求。他指出，现代社会中的人们习惯于被"喂养"一切，绝大多数用户甚至不会去探索手机的设置选项，更不用说去定制软件。他以Unix为例，指出尽管技术上强大，但大多数人并不使用它，而更倾向于使用功能繁多但可能臃肿的软件产品。

• eternityforest表示自己倾向于避免使用需要修改的软件或库。他认为，手动合并更新、检查更新以及编写集成脚本等工作会增加额外的工作量。此外，未经完整审核或测试的软件可能会带来风险，因此他更愿意使用经过验证的解决方案。

• senkora提到这种讨论与Suckless哲学有重叠之处，引用了Suckless.org的哲学，暗示有些人确实欣赏并追求简约、可定制的软件设计理念。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于用户是否愿意并且有能力对软件进行定制。vivzkestrel强调了大多数用户的惰性和对简便解决方案的偏好，而senkora则指出了有一部分用户群体确实欣赏和追求可定制性。

• eternityforest的观点提供了一个实际操作中的顾虑，即修改软件可能带来的额外工作量和技术挑战，这对普通用户来说可能不太实际。

• 引用的Suckless哲学为讨论提供了一个具体的例子，展示了确实存在一个社区和哲学支持并实践软件定制和简约设计。

总结来看，讨论的核心在于软件定制化的可行性和实际需求，不同用户群体对软件复杂性和可定制性的偏好，以及这种做法在实际应用中的优缺点。

44274048.article_content:
on the usability of editable software
I’m aware of two occasions on which Knuth advised editing existing code, as opposed to simply using it. One mention is in
this interview
, advocating for “re-editable” code instead of the fashionable reusable code, although it doesn’t amount to much more than that statement. In
Coders at Work
he describes a system of working that’s basically patch and diff. He writes a program, the master version that works for him, and ships it out. People receive and it and then modify it with change files so it works for them.
This is a rather different way to approach the needs of multiple users than the industry standard, which is to incorporate all the changes and variations anybody could want into a single version for everybody. If we consider some sort 80/20 rule where 80% of the users need 20% of the features, but it’s always a different 20%, this will have quite the impact on the size of our code base. I think that’s rather an exaggeration, with 15% features shared by nearly all users, and some variation in the extra. But conceptually, we could be shipping much smaller, simpler software if users could modify it to their own ends.
Some time ago I bought a dining room table and chairs. The first thing I did, immediately after taking delivery, was drive the chairs over to another business to be reupholstered. The originals weren’t bad, but they weren’t to my taste, and there weren’t any other chairs matching all of desired, affordable, and critically, available. So I bought what was available, then I had them modified, because that’s something you can do to things. Modify them.
Software can be modified as well. Or could be, if we didn’t go to such lengths to avoid it. There’s this notion that a software program needs to be finished, and polished, and work out of the box. That end users cannot be expected to be programmers. I’ll note that I did not reupholster my chairs by myself. They were basically functional as shipped, which certainly should be true of software as well, but I wasn’t forced to upgrade them entirely by myself. I could probably learn to be an upholsterer, but it was not necessary. Neither did I have to work with a specially trained upholsterer familiar with this model of chair. I took one sample over to the shop, he looked it over, and said yeah, I can do this no problem.
There are two forces at work leading to an unfortunate feedback loop in which software is difficult to modify, and then seeks to avoid modification, further complicating it. First, we don’t consider modification as a positive outcome for the user. We seek to package everything up to avoid local changes. Second, the way software is deployed causes local changes to be very expensive, creating pressure to push everything upstream. Neither of these must be the case however.
What if we made software with the expectation that end users would make at least a few changes? This would greatly simplify things. We don’t need to worry about every use case. Or even most use cases, really. Just provide the essential features. But isn’t that creating more work for end users? Not if the program is easy enough to work with. As anyone familiar with software development knows, the difficulty of adding new features or modifying existing ones grows very quickly, much faster than linearly, with the total number of features. They interfere with one another. By reducing the number of shipped features, we reduce the difficulty of modification. Anybody can do it (or have somebody do it for them).
The more users we try to appease out of the box, the harder things become for those we haven’t served yet. A more rigorous analysis would attempt to model costs and benefits, do the math, etc. I’ll leave it at noting that the combination of the 80/20 rule and superlinear complexity growth means we probably aren’t amortizing as much effort as we would hope by adding every feature to a single code base.
Another consequence of continuously adding features is that local changes become difficult to maintain. Every new release, local changes need to be merged and updated. The more releases there are, the faster the treadmill spins. The more each release changes, the steeper the treadmill incline. Very rarely do I see new development consider how local changes might be impacted.
An alternative approach to simpler editable software is complex programs with plugins. Witness browsers. Nobody wants to modify the browser itself, but maybe there’s a plugin, or extension, to do what you want. Unless the browser says your adblock list is too big. Or says the API you want is obsolete. And then going back into the main source tree to fix it so your extension still works the way you want is a major undertaking. There are other costs with large customizable programs as well. How often do we hear browser trouble, have you tried deleting your profile? Nobody knows what goes wrong, except it happens, and then you start over until next time.

44274048.article_summary: 文章讨论了软件可编辑性的重要性，提出了与当前追求“可重用代码”不同的观点，主张“可再编辑代码”。作者以Knuth的观点为例，指出可以让用户根据自己需求修改代码，而不是在单一版本中包含所有可能的功能。这种方法可以使软件更小、更简单，因为只需提供核心功能，而非满足所有用户需求。目前软件开发常忽视用户修改的需求，导致软件难以更改，并形成恶性循环。作者建议设计时考虑用户可能进行的修改，从而简化软件，并减少因功能增加带来的复杂性。此外，插件和扩展虽然提供一定灵活性，但也带来维护和兼容性问题。最终，文章呼吁重新思考软件设计，使其更易于修改和定制。

data.title: Inside the Apollo “8-Ball” FDAI (Flight Director / Attitude Indicator)
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了阿波罗登月任务中用于显示飞船姿态的FDAI（飞行总监/姿态指示器）的运作原理。FDAI通过一个被称为"8-ball"的球体显示飞船的姿态，球体可以绕三轴（滚转、俯仰和偏航）旋转。该仪器还通过三根黄色指针指示 astronauts 应如何操纵飞船，另有三根指针显示飞船的旋转速度。FDAI内部使用三个马达分别控制球体绕三轴的旋转，球体在“赤道”处牢固连接，并通过外部壳体实现第三轴的旋转。Lunar Module 拥有两个FDAI，一个供指挥官使用，另一个供登月舱驾驶员使用，每个FDAI可以从多个来源获取数据并显示姿态信息和旋转速率。仪表通过不同的开关选择显示模式和数据源，并由阿波罗制导计算机等设备提供误差指示。

44277051.article_content:
During the Apollo flights to the Moon, the astronauts observed the spacecraft's orientation on a special instrument
called the FDAI (Flight Director / Attitude Indicator).
This instrument showed the spacecraft's attitude—its orientation—by rotating a ball.
This ball was nicknamed the "8-ball" because it was black (albeit only on one side).
The instrument also acted as a flight director, using three yellow needles to indicate how the astronauts should maneuver
the spacecraft. Three more pointers showed how fast the spacecraft was rotating.
An Apollo FDAI (Flight Director/Attitude Indicator) with the case removed. This FDAI is on its side to avoid crushing the needles.
Since the spacecraft rotates along three axes (roll, pitch, and yaw), the ball also rotates along three axes.
It's not obvious how the ball can rotate to an arbitrary orientation while remaining attached.
In this article, I look inside an FDAI from Apollo that was repurposed for a Space Shuttle simulator
1
and explain how it operates. (Spoiler: the ball mechanism is firmly attached
at the "equator" and rotates in two axes. What you see is two hollow shells around the ball mechanism that spin around the third axis.)
The FDAI in Apollo
For the missions to the Moon, the Lunar Module had two FDAIs, as shown below: one on the left for the Commander (Neil Armstrong in Apollo 11) and
one on the right for the Lunar Module Pilot (Buzz Aldrin in Apollo 11).
With their size and central positions, the FDAIs dominate the instrument panel, a sign of their importance.
(The Command Module for Apollo also had two FDAIs, but with a different design; I won't discuss them here.
2
)
The instrument panel in the Lunar Module. From
Apollo 15 Lunar Module
, NASA, S71-40761. If you're looking for the DSKY, it is in the bottom center, just out of the picture.
Each Lunar Module FDAI could display inputs from multiple sources, selected by switches on the panel.
3
The ball could display attitude from either the
Inertial Measurement Unit
or from the backup Abort Guidance System, selected by the "ATTITUDE MON" toggle switch next to either FDAI.
The pitch attitude could also be supplied by an electromechanical unit called ORDEAL (Orbital Rate Display Earth And Lunar)
that simulates a circular orbit.
The error indications came from the Apollo Guidance Computer, the Abort Guidance System, the landing radar,
or the rendezvous radar (controlled by the "RATE/ERROR MON" switches).
The pitch, roll, and yaw rate displays were driven by the Rate Gyro Assembly (RGA).
The rate indications were scaled by a switch below the FDAI, selecting 25°/sec or 5°/sec.
The FDAI mechanism
The ball inside the indicator shows rotation around three axes.
I'll first explain these axes in the context of an aircraft, since the axes of a spacecraft are more arbitrary.
4
The roll axis indicates the aircraft's angle if it rolls side-to-side along its axis of flight, raising one wing
and lowering the other.
Thus, the indicator shows the tilt of the horizon as the aircraft rolls.
The pitch axis indicates the aircraft's angle if it pitches up or down, with the indicator showing the horizon
moving down or up in response.
Finally, the yaw axis indicates the compass direction that the aircraft is heading,
changing as the aircraft turns left or right.
(A typical aircraft attitude indicator omits yaw.)
I'll illustrate how the FDAI rotates the ball in three axes, using an orange as an example.
Imagine pinching the horizontal axis between two fingers with your arm extended.
Rotating your arm will roll the ball counter-clockwise or clockwise (red arrow).
In the FDAI, this rotation is accomplished by a motor turning the frame that holds the ball.
For pitch, the ball rotates forward or backward around the horizontal axis (yellow arrow).
The FDAI has a motor inside the ball to produce this rotation.
Yaw is a bit more difficult to envision: imagine hemisphere-shaped shells attached to the top and bottom shafts.
When a motor rotates these shells (green arrow), the hemispheres will rotate, even though
the ball mechanism (the orange) remains stationary.
A sphere, showing the three axes.
The diagram below shows the mechanism inside the FDAI.
The indicator uses three motors to move the ball.
The roll motor is attached to the FDAI's frame, while the pitch and yaw motors are inside the ball.
The roll motor rotates the roll gimbal through gears, causing the ball to rotate clockwise or counterclockwise.
The roll gimbal is attached to the ball mechanism at two points along the "equator";
these two points define the pitch axis.
Numerous wires on the roll gimbal enter the ball along the pitch axis.
The roll control transformer provides position feedback, as will be explained below.
The main components inside the FDAI.
Removing the hemispherical shells reveals the
mechanism inside the ball.
When the roll gimbal is rotated, this mechanism rotates with it.
The pitch motor causes the ball mechanism to rotate around the pitch axis.

data.title: Peeling the Covers Off Germany's Exascale "Jupiter" Supercomputer
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: Jupiter是德国Forschungszentrum Jülich设施中首台达到百亿亿次级的超级计算机，采用混合CPU-GPU架构，由Eviden和ParTec建造。其主要计算性能来自GPU加速模块，在2025年6月的Top500排名中位列第四。尽管最初希望使用欧洲公司设计的自定义芯片，但Jupiter主要基于Nvidia的硬件。其通用集群模块采用SiPearl的Rhea1 Arm服务器CPU，拥有超过1300个节点，每个节点配备两个80核的Rhea1芯片，并配有64GB HBM内存。Rhea1原计划于2024年6月推出，预计今年晚些时候交付。Jupiter的GPU加速模块使用Nvidia的Grace G100 Arm服务器CPU和Hopper H200 GPU，每个节点包含两个计算模块，通过NVLink端口连接，提供高带宽数据传输。该系统标志着欧洲在高性能计算领域迈向芯片独立的一步，但仍依赖Nvidia技术。

44255770.article_content:
The newest of the exascale-class supercomputer to be profiled in the Top500 rankings in the June list is the long-awaited “Jupiter” system at Forschungszentrum Jülich facility in Germany. We finally have a sense of how this hybrid CPU-GPU machine will perform, although some of the details on its configuration are still not nailed down publicly.
Jupiter is the first exascale system to be completed under the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking of the European Union, and the fact that it is not using a custom CPU and XPU created by European companies, as was originally hoped, and is basically an Nvidia machine top to middle – bottom would include Nvidia storage, which it hasn’t acquired yet but will – speaks volumes about difficult it is to start from scratch to achieve chip independence for Europe. But, the Universal Cluster module will be based on the “Rhea1” Arm server CPU created by SiPearl, which is a step in the direction of independence for European HPC.
The Jupiter machine is built by Eviden, the HPC division of Atos that was going to be spun out but which the company has had second – and good – thoughts about doing, and ParTec, the German HPC system designer and installer.
Like its predecessor, the “Jewels” system that was first deployed in 2018 and upgraded a few times over the years, Jupiter is a hybrid supercomputer with blocks of CPU and GPU compute with other kinds of storage and acceleration blocks linked into it. With Jewels, the Cluster Module was installed first, based on Intel “Skylake” Xeon SP processors linked with 100 Gb/sec EDR InfiniBand from the then-independent Mellanox Technologies with everything installed in a BullSequana X1000 system from Eviden. In 2020, a BullSequana XH2000 system loaded up with AMD “Rome” Epyc CPUs and Nvidia “Ampere” GPU accelerators and called a Booster Module, was added to Jewels using 200 Gb/sec HDR InfiniBand.
Here is the honeycomb diagram for Jupiter, showing its modular components:
The vast majority of floating point and integer performance in Jupiter is, of course, in the GPU Booster module, which was taken for a spin using the High Performance LINPACK benchmark commonly used to rank supercomputer throughput and which
placed this Jupiter Booster module in the number four position on the June 2025 Top500 rankings
of supposedly HPC-centric systems.
The Universal Cluster will have more than CPU-only 1,300 nodes based on a pair of Rhea1 chips with 80 cores each based on the “Zeus” Neoverse V1 cores. These are the same V1 cores used in the “Graviton3” Arm chip designed by Amazon Web Services, which have a pair of 256-bit SVE vector engines. Each Rhea1 has a bank of 64 GB of HBM memory, the same fast but not fat memory used on GPU and XPU accelerators these days. As far as we know, the Rhea1 chip
was delayed back in June 2024
and is expected sometime later this year for FZJ. Some variant of SiPearl Arm CPU – maybe Rhea1 but also maybe its Rhea2 kicker – will also be employed in the second exascale system in Europe, called “Alice Recoque” and set to be hosted in France and presumably also to be built by Eviden. The Alice Recoque system has a budget of €542 million ($580.2 million), which includes money for the system, the facility, and its power and cooling.
This Universal Cluster is expected to have a mere 5 petaflops of FP64 performance running the HPL benchmark, which probably puts it at somewhere around 7 petaflops at peak theoretical performance. This is tiny compared to the Jupiter GPU Booster module that was tested for the June Top500 list.
The Jupiter GPU Booster node is based on a unique four-way clustering of Nvidia “Grace” G100 Arm server CPUs, which essentially uses four “Hopper” H200 GPUs as NUMA node controllers to link four CPUs and four GPUs into a more hefty cluster of eight compute engines working in harmony.
For those of you who didn’t see it
when we wrote about the Jupiter nodes back in September 2024
, here is a block diagram of the Jupiter GPU Booster node, which has a pair of sleds, each with a quad of Grace-Hopper modules linked by their main memories using direct NVLink ports off the CPUs and GPUs. Here is a block diagram of each node:
The H200 GPUs have 96 GB of HBM3 memory each, with 4 TB/sec of bandwidth across each accelerator. The single NVLink 4 ports that cross-link the four H200s together provide 300 GB/sec of bandwidth between them (150 GB/sec in each direction). Moreover, each Hopper GPU can communicate with the Grace CPU that hangs off of it at 600 GB/sec (300 GB/sec per direction) and to the other three CPUs in the quad complex at 100 GB/sec (50 GB/sec). Each CPU has a PCI-Express 5.0 port that reaches out to the 200 GB/sec ConnectX-6 SmartNIC. (With the “Blackwell” GPU designs, the GPUs link directly to the SmartNICs rather than having to go through the Grace CPUs.)
There are two compute sleds, each with a pair of Grace-Hopper superchips, in each Jupiter node, and there are also pair of dual-port 400 Gb/sec ConnectX-7 NDR InfiniBand

data.title: We investigated Amsterdam's attempt to build a 'fair' fraud detection model
data.author: troelsSteegin
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了阿姆斯特丹市开发的一种机器学习模型，旨在识别需要进一步调查的福利申请。该模型使用了一种名为可解释提升机（EBM）的算法，通过分析申请者的行为和特征来预测“调查价值”，并生成风险评分。尽管模型没有直接使用性别或种族等敏感信息，但仍可能通过其他变量间接关联到特定群体。文章指出，尽管阿姆斯特丹在开发过程中努力确保模型的透明和公平，但其他地方如鹿特丹和法国社会保障机构在类似系统中忽视了对偏见的审查，导致对弱势群体的歧视。文章还提到，欧盟和纽约等地已开始通过立法限制高风险AI的使用，但构建公平的AI工具仍面临复杂挑战。最终，文章强调了在AI决策中实现公平的现实困难和持续努力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕阿姆斯特丹福利欺诈检测模型的公平性、有效性及其实施过程的讨论，包括模型中的偏差、公平定义的权衡以及模型性能问题。

不同观点：
• **tbrownaw** 和其他一些评论者认为，模型设计者意识到某些特征可能成为人口统计群体的代理变量，导致不公平的结果。这种不公平源于对不同群体关注度的权衡，即关注某一维度的公平（如减少基于种族/民族的差异）可能会损害其他维度的表现。这种权衡在模型中是不可避免的。
  
• **thatguymike** 和 **LorenPechtel** 对阿姆斯特丹项目的整体执行表示肯定。他们认为项目在伦理上建立了防护措施，并在无法满足公平标准时不部署模型，这是一种负责任的做法。然而，**LorenPechtel** 质疑过分关注“公平”是否必要，认为更应关注最小化错误率（假阳性和假阴性）。

• **GardenLetter27** 提出，虽然模型中未明确引用性别、种族等受保护的特征，但模型设计者应意识到这些特征可能通过其他相关变量成为代理变量。这并非种族主义，而是基于贝叶斯定理的正常现象。

• **bananaquant** 和 **BonoboIO** 批评模型的性能，认为模型的准确性不高（约67%的正预测准确率），其性能远低于高风险场景下应有的表现。他们质疑模型的实际效果，尤其是与系统有效性相关的指标（如真实阳性率、召回率）未被提及。

• **3abiton** 和 **octo888** 则关注模型复现性和数据处理问题。**3abiton** 指出，城市无法完全复现其分析结果，且模型偏差数据和已发布报告存在无法解释的差异，这让人质疑实验的可靠性。**octo888** 建议在标题中加入“福利”一词以更准确地描述情境。

• **ncruces** 和 **londons_explore** 提出更极端的观点。他们认为，在这些情况下实现完全公平是不可能的，主张采用完全随机的方式或通过补偿机制来减轻被错误调查者的负担。

补充讨论：
• **tomp** 和 **Jimmc414** 强调，不同公平标准之间的冲突是数学上的现实问题，难以同时满足所有标准。训练模型时，过去的人类决策偏差不可避免地被引入模型中，从而影响模型的公平性。

• **zeroCalories** 关注“重新加权”的实际操作，询问这是否意味着对某些群体的错误分类进行更多惩罚，或确保各群体在数据中均匀分布。

争议焦点：
• 模型中的公平性定义和权衡：是否应优先考虑某些群体的利益，即使这可能损害其他群体的表现。
• 模型的实际效果和有效性：在准确性不足的情况下，模型的部署价值和意义受到质疑。
• 数据处理和复现性问题：实验的可靠性和结果的可信度受到质疑。

总结：讨论围绕模型的公平性、准确性和数据处理的可靠性展开，各方对如何实现公平、模型性能的标准以及实际操作中的问题提出了不同见解。

The Limits of Ethical AI
June 11, 2025
How the model works
Training the Model
Fairness Definitions
The City’s First Model
The City’s ‘Debiased’ Model
The Debiased Model is Deployed in a Pilot
Fairness Tradeoffs
Model Performance
Technical Details
Limitations
For the past four years, Lighthouse has investigated welfare fraud detection algorithms deployed in five European countries. Our investigations have found evidence that these systems discriminated against vulnerable groups with oftentimes steep consequences for people’s lives.
Governments and companies deploying these systems often show little regard for the biases they perpetrate against vulnerable groups. The city of Rotterdam told us that it had never run code designed to test whether its model was disproportionately flagging vulnerable groups. France’s social security agency, CNAF, confirmed to us that it had never audited its model for bias.
In January of 2023, three months before publishing our investigation into Rotterdam’s risk scoring algorithm, we sent a public records request to the city of Amsterdam, one of Europe’s most progressive capitals. Among other things, we asked for documents, code and data relating to a similar system Amsterdam had been developing. Given that we had fought over a year to obtain these types of material in other investigations, we were surprised when the city immediately complied with our request.
The materials disclosed by the city were related to a machine learning model it was developing in order to predict which of the city’s residents were most likely to have submitted an incorrect application for welfare. At the time of our public records request, the model was still in development. The overall development goal for the model, according to the city’s internal documentation, was to have fewer welfare applicants investigated, but a higher share of those investigated rejected. Internal documents also emphasized two other aims: avoid bias against vulnerable groups, and outperform human caseworkers.
After reading through the documentation, it quickly became clear to us why the city had been so forthcoming. The city had gone to significant lengths in order to develop a model that was transparent and treated vulnerable groups fairly.
We wanted to investigate whether the city of Amsterdam had succeeded in developing a fair model. Over the course of eight months, we ran a series of our own tests on the model and data containing real world outcomes for people flagged as suspicious by the model. When it came to the outcome data, the city ran our own tests locally and returned aggregate results in order to comply with European data protection laws.
The past five years have seen a number of regulatory efforts to reign in harmful uses of AI. The EU AI Act, passed in 2024, will require AI systems deemed “high risk” to be registered with the European Commission. In New York City, employers have been prohibited from screening employees using AI without conducting bias audits since July 2023. Meanwhile, the private sector, academics and multilateral institutions have produced a number of responsible AI frameworks. In taking on this investigation, we wanted to look ahead and understand the thorny reality of building a fair AI tool that makes consequential decisions about people’s lives.
The code and data underlying our analysis can be found on our
Github
.
How the model works
The City of Amsterdam’s model aimed to identify applications for further investigation. Staff members check for applications that contain mistakes and redirect any concerning applications to an investigator. The model is designed to replicate this first screening.
A flagged application is not automatically rejected. However, investigators are empowered to request a beneficiary’s bank statements, summon them for meetings, and even visit their homes. Past reporting, including our own, has shown how these investigations can be a stressful or even traumatising experience.
The model uses a type of algorithm called an Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM). EBMs prioritize explainability — the degree to which an AI algorithm is understandable instead of being a confusing “black box” of abstract mathematical processes. Amsterdam’s EBM model predicts ‘investigation worthiness’ based on variables that measure welfare applicants’ behavior and characteristics, features.
Model predictions are based on 15 features. None of these features explicitly referred to an applicant’s gender or racial background, as well as other demographic characteristics protected by anti-discrimination law. But the model designers were aware that features could be correlated with demographic groups in a way that would make them proxies.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Commodore 64及其冻结卡带的技术原理、实现方式以及相关硬件的讨论，同时涉及与其他平台（如Atari 8-bit和Amiga）的比较。

不同观点：
• michalpleban认为，运行在Commodore 64上的软件可以通过自行触发NMI中断，并保持NMI线路低电平，从而防止被冻结技术中断。他具体解释了通过使用第二个CIA芯片来实现这一点的机制。
• erwincoumans回顾了过去使用Power Cartridge的经历，并提到自己曾通过逆向工程实现了类似功能，如保存/恢复游戏、加速加载和截图功能，展示了当时对硬件卡带的深入研究和改造。
• sfjailbird回忆了自制冻结卡带的历史，指出当时这类卡带的制造和流通情况，强调了这些卡带的实用性和受欢迎程度，尽管当时对背后的技术细节不甚了解。
• classichasclass对比了不同类型的冻结卡带，表达了对FC3接口的喜爱，但指出在NTSC系统上使用时遇到的问题，因此更常使用其他替代卡带如ICEPIC或Super Snapshot。
• daitangio对Commodore 64代码的复杂性和精简性表示惊叹，强调了在极少字节数下实现复杂功能的编程技巧。
• predictsoft将Commodore 64的冻结功能与Amiga 1200上的Action Replay软盘功能作对比，指出Amiga可以通过软件直接利用高地址空间加载，而无需额外硬件支持，暗示软件解决方案有时更为灵活。
• TMWNN讨论了Atari 8-bit系统上没有冻结卡带的原因，推测是由于缺乏Ultimax-style bypass机制，同时提到Atari 8-bit的设计使得FujiNet可以无需像Commodore系统那样的变通方法或缺点，暗示了不同硬件架构对类似功能实现的影响。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了不同平台（Commodore 64、Atari 8-bit、Amiga）之间的技术差异和实现类似功能的不同方法，特别是硬件和软件解决方案的对比。
• 冻结卡带的技术不仅涉及到防止程序被中断，还涉及到快速加载、保存游戏等实用功能，展示了当时用户对C64等平台的深度定制能力。
• 争议的焦点在于冻结技术的实现方法和可行性，特别是软件是否能够主动防止被冻结，这引发了对NMI中断机制的深入讨论。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章旨在揭露和澄清有关HDR（高动态范围）和SDR（标准动态范围）之间的一些误解和技术细节。文章首先介绍了基础概念，包括人类对色调的相对感知以及颜色空间的理解。随后，文章比较了SDR和HDR的颜色空间，讨论了两者转换的解决方案。文章还分析了市场上对HDR的一些误导性宣传，如效率问题、色域误解以及创作者意图与自动化处理的冲突。最后，文章提出了应对建议，并总结了要点，强调色调的艺术性而非纯粹的技术性处理。

主要讨论点：关于视频色彩理论和HDR与SDR技术的分析和讨论

不同观点：
• **[_wire_]**: 认为视频对色彩理论的应用进行了扎实的概述，但指出视频在开篇未能明确提出要辩驳的论点。视频的核心是比较SDR和HDR，指出HDR提供了更高的保真度，但最终视觉效果的价值仍取决于创作者的创意。同时，强调了人类视觉适应的动态范围差异，并通过对比100:1和数十亿:1的感知窗口解释了HDR的优势。

• **[dcrazy]**: 对视频中颜色空间和术语的简化表示不满，指出Yedlin在RGB三元组和颜色空间坐标之间的混淆，并强调Rec. 2100不仅定义了颜色空间，还定义了传输函数（PQ和HLG），这些细节在视频中被忽略了。不过，对视频中的一些类比（如英尺/米转换）表示赞赏。

• **[nayuki]**: 更关注视频的技术传输质量，称赞视频的无缓冲加载速度和用户界面响应速度，对比YouTube的缓慢体验，认为多亿级公司提供的用户体验不如一个简单的视频文件。

• **[IshKebab]**: 认为视频过长且没有在开头明确指出要辩驳的内容，希望得到简明的总结。

• **[sansseriff]**: 对Yedlin的视频表示赞赏，但希望他能分享代码以促进开源色彩分级软件的开发，指出由于色彩分级工具多为专有，科学研究的开放性受限。

• **[virtualritz]**: 提到在Android设备上观看视频时遇到的全屏退出问题，认为这是一个奇怪的Chrome/Android bug。

• **[magicalhippo]**: 快速浏览视频后，感觉视频内容类似于讨论24位音频是否必要，并分享了自己从SDR到HDR的早期技术体验，希望看到更高动态范围的显示效果。

• **[ttoinou]**: 认为Yedlin指出的SDR输入在某些情况下与HDR相似是显而易见的，但强调HDR不仅是一个数学转换公式，更是一种新的交流方式。同时，对Yedlin的“所有图像都适用”的观点表示怀疑，认为HDR为创意提供了更广阔的色彩空间。

• **[autobodie]**: 对视频内容表示强烈赞同，提到阅读过相关书籍，认为HDR和SDR的问题与ACES有很大重叠，并将广泛分享此视频。

• **[FrostKiwi]**: 对视频使用Nuke完成表示赞赏，认为其体现了技术和艺术的完美结合。

• **[naikrovek]**: 将30位色彩与16位色彩的过渡进行对比，认为HDR的销售宣传夸大了实际视觉差异，指出显示器制造商通过HDR模式锁定某些功能以促进销售。

• **[empiricus]**: 认为应从接近现实的捕捉开始，然后进行创意处理，SDR类似于黑白电影，而HDR有潜力实现更真实的视觉效果，但目前电影制作者尚未充分利用。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于HDR与SDR的实际视觉差异以及HDR技术的必要性。部分观众认为HDR提供了更大的创作空间和更高的保真度，而另一些观众则认为这种差异被夸大，且HDR技术可能被商家利用以促进销售。

• 视频的技术细节和术语使用也引发了讨论，部分观众认为Yedlin在解释颜色空间和传输函数时过于简化，导致信息传递不够准确。

• 视频的技术传输质量和用户体验得到了部分观众的好评，尤其是与YouTube的对比。

• 开源色彩分级软件的提议得到了关注，但受限于当前专有工具的广泛使用，这一提议实现起来可能面临挑战。

data.title: Have a damaged painting? Restore it in just hours with an AI-generated “mask”
data.author: WithinReason
data.article_summary: 麻省理工学院的研究生Alex Kachkine开发了一种使用数字构造膜物理修复原始画作的新方法。该方法通过打印极薄的聚合物膜，形成一个可以对齐并粘贴到画作上的“面具”，以覆盖和修复受损区域，且该膜可以轻松移除。这种技术可以在几个小时内完成传统修复方法需要数周甚至更长时间的工作。例如，Kachkine在3.5小时内修复了一幅15世纪的油画，而传统方法可能需要更久。同时，数字记录可以保存修复细节，供未来修复者参考。不过，Kachkine也强调，任何修复都应与了解画作历史和来源的保护专家协商，以确保修复的伦理性和适当性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：艺术品修复中的技术应用（特别是AI）及其伦理问题

不同观点：
• **Daub**：对艺术品修复持批评态度，认为过去的修复项目往往造成了对艺术品的破坏。他举例提到西斯廷教堂天花板的修复项目，认为选择了错误的假设（即米开朗基罗没有对壁画进行任何修正），从而破坏了原作。他还提到维多利亚时代对雕塑的过度清洗以及现代修复者根据客户喜好更改艺术品元素的做法，认为这些都是对艺术品的不当处理。

• **contravariant**：对修复方法的兴趣大于AI本身，但认为声称使用AI可能是为了获得资金支持。这暗示了技术应用中的营销和资金需求问题。

• **bee_rider**：提出艺术家原始意图与修复之间的关系，认为是否应该恢复艺术品是一个值得讨论的问题。同时，也提到艺术品随着时间老化所带来的历史故事，可能不应仅由艺术家决定是否修复。

• **t43562**：建议可以完全不触碰原作，而是通过复制品进行展示和保护，从而避免对原作的任何潜在破坏。

• **matt3210**：质疑是否需要通过AI生成新画作，并提出如果大部分画面被掩盖，那么原作是否还能被称为画作的问题。

• **ecocentrik**：认为即使AI修复技术完美无缺，改变艺术品的展示方式（如包裹艺术品）也会影响观众的体验，从而改变艺术的本质。

• **zelphirkalt**：对AI在修复中的实际作用持怀疑态度，认为大部分工作可能是机械性的，AI可能只涉及颜色推断或遮罩预测。同时质疑谁来负责历史准确性的确认。

• **omoikane**：担心数字记录的长期可读性问题，提出即使有数字记录，也需要定期更新以确保其可用性。

• **zelikane**：引用xkcd漫画，幽默地指出技术修复中可能出现的长期问题。

补充讨论：
• **not_your_mentat**：以幽默的方式提到可以在损坏的部分填充“无象”（no elephants），暗示修复过程中可能会加入不合适的元素。

• **amelius**：幽默地表达了对AI生成不准确部分（如七根手指的手）的担忧，反映了人们对AI技术在艺术领域应用的潜在不信任。

争议焦点：
• 修复技术（尤其是AI）是否应该在艺术品修复中广泛应用，以及如何平衡艺术家的原始意图、历史故事和现代观众的观赏需求。
• 艺术品修复的伦理问题，包括是否应该完全避免对原作的任何改动，以及谁有权决定修复的方式和程度。

Art restoration takes steady hands and a discerning eye. For centuries, conservators have restored paintings by identifying areas needing repair, then mixing an exact shade to fill in one area at a time. Often, a painting can have thousands of tiny regions requiring individual attention. Restoring a single painting can take anywhere from a few weeks to over a decade.
In recent years, digital restoration tools have opened a route to creating virtual representations of original, restored works. These tools apply techniques of computer vision, image recognition, and color matching, to generate a “digitally restored” version of a painting relatively quickly.
Still, there has been no way to translate digital restorations directly onto an original work, until now. In a
paper
appearing today in the journal
Nature
, Alex Kachkine, a mechanical engineering graduate student at MIT, presents a new method he’s developed to physically apply a digital restoration directly onto an original painting.
The restoration is printed on a very thin polymer film, in the form of a mask that can be aligned and adhered to an original painting. It can also be easily removed. Kachkine says that a digital file of the mask can be stored and referred to by future conservators, to see exactly what changes were made to restore the original painting.
“Because there’s a digital record of what mask was used, in 100 years, the next time someone is working with this, they’ll have an extremely clear understanding of what was done to the painting,” Kachkine says. “And that’s never really been possible in conservation before.”
As a demonstration, he applied the method to a highly damaged 15th century oil painting. The method automatically identified 5,612 separate regions in need of repair, and filled in these regions using 57,314 different colors. The entire process, from start to finish, took 3.5 hours, which he estimates is about 66 times faster than traditional restoration methods.
Kachkine acknowledges that, as with any restoration project, there are ethical issues to consider, in terms of whether a restored version is an appropriate representation of an artist’s original style and intent. Any application of his new method, he says, should be done in consultation with conservators with knowledge of a painting’s history and origins.

• **not_your_mentat**：以幽默的方式提到可以在损坏的部分填充“无象”（no elephants），暗示修复过程中可能会加入不合适的元素。

• **amelius**：幽默地表达了对AI生成不准确部分（如七根手指的手）的担忧，反映了人们对AI技术在艺术领域应用的潜在不信任。

争议焦点：
• 修复技术（尤其是AI）是否应该在艺术品修复中广泛应用，以及如何平衡艺术家的原始意图、历史故事和现代观众的观赏需求。
• 艺术品修复的伦理问题，包括是否应该完全避免对原作的任何改动，以及谁有权决定修复的方式和程度。

data.title: Infinite Grid of Resistors
data.author: niklasbuschmann
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了一个经典的电阻网格谜题，该网格由无限延伸的方形晶格组成，每对相邻节点之间有一个电阻R。文章主要探讨如何计算相邻节点之间的有效电阻。通过考虑电流场的对称性和叠加原理，文章得出相邻节点间的有效电阻为R/2。这种方法类似于电偶极子的电势场分析，利用了拉普拉斯方程的对称性。然而，文章也指出，该推导依赖于一些假设，例如电流在“无限远处”的行为，而这些假设并未完全严谨证明。特别是，将电流注入无限网格的设想存在问题，因为理论上节点到无限远的电阻是无限大的。尽管如此，通过简单对称性得出的结果R/2与其他方法验证结果一致。文章最后提到，要使论证更严谨，可以考虑有限大小的网格。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于无限电阻网格问题的相关性和实际应用的讨论，包括电阻网格的理论分析、实际工程中的应用及其教学价值。

不同观点：
• [bgnnn] 认为无限电阻网格问题与实际世界问题相关，特别是在集成电路中的硅基板噪声耦合问题。他强调了网格结构在实际工程中的应用，例如通过分布基板接点来收集噪声电流。
• [neepi] 指出，从实际测量的角度来看，问题在于如何测量，尤其是在考虑分布式电感和电容元件时。数学角度和工程角度存在分歧。
• [kayson] 认为更具教育意义的做法是讨论立方体对角电阻问题，这有助于建立电路对称性和基尔霍夫定律（KCL）等直觉，而不是专注于无限网格问题。
• [bilsbie] 提出一个衍生问题，即为什么不通过减小电线直径来制造电阻，认为这样可能比将电流转化为热量更有效率。
• [TheOtherHobbes] 认为无限网格问题是一个无意义的问题，因为在数学上会导致不确定的无穷大/无穷大结果，建议将时间用于更有意义的问题。

补充讨论：
• [dogman1050] 指出该问题可以视为“薄层电阻”的特例，并提供了一个维基百科链接。
• [praptak] 对对称性和叠加原理的应用提出疑问，质疑为何两个节点的电流可以简单地视为两个单独节点电流的和。
• [bilsbie] 进一步提问，为什么真空不能被视为一个无限电阻网格。
• [quibono] 对对称性和叠加解释中的方向性选择提出疑问，不明白为何一个方向与其他两个方向不同。
• [pyman] 提供了关于无限电阻网格的一个具体结果，指出相邻点之间的电阻大约是三分之一电阻值。
• [at_a_remove] 分享了与渗透理论相关的实际项目经验，描述了通过导电墨水制作不同网格并测量电阻的实验过程。

争议焦点：
• 无限电阻网格问题是否具有实际工程相关性及其在教学中的价值。
• 对称性和叠加原理在分析无限电阻网格中的适用性和解释方式。
• 实际测量中的可行性和理论分析的复杂性。

这些讨论展示了理论问题在实际应用和教学中的不同视角，以及对复杂电路问题分析方法的深入探讨。

Resistors
Remain, remain thou here,
While
sense can keep it on. And, sweetest, fairest,
As
I my poor self did exchange for you,
To
your so infinite loss, so in our trifles
I
still win of you: for my sake wear this...
Shakespeare
There is a well-known puzzle based on the premise of an
infinite grid of resistors connecting adjacent nodes of a square lattice. A
small portion of such a grid is illustrated below.
Between every pair of adjacent nodes is a resistance R,
and were told that this grid of resistors extends to infinity in all
direction, and were asked to determine the effective resistance between two
adjacent nodes, or, more generally, between any two specified nodes of the
lattice.
For adjacent nodes, the usual solution of this puzzle is
to consider the current flow field as the sum of two components, one being
the flow field of a grid with current injected into a single node, and the
other being the flow field of a grid with current extracted from a single
(adjacent) node. The symmetry of the two individual cases then enables us to
infer the flow rates through the immediately adjacent resistors, and hence we
can conclude (as explained in more detail below) that the effective
resistance between two adjacent nodes is R/2. This solution has a certain
intuitive plausibility, since its similar to how the potential field of an
electric dipole can be expressed as the sum of the fields of a positive and a
negative charge, each of which is spherically symmetrical about its
respective charge. Just as the electric potential satisfies the Laplace equation, the voltages of the grid nodes satisfy the discrete from of the Laplace equation, which is to say, the voltage at each node is the average of the voltages
of the four surrounding nodes. Its also easy to see that solutions are
additive, in the sense that the sum of any two solutions for given boundary
conditions is a solution for the sum of the boundary conditions.
If we accept the premise of an infinite grid of resistors,
along with some tacit assumption about the behavior of the voltages and
currents at infinity, and if we accept the idea that we can treat the
current fields for the positive and negative nodes separately, and that
applying a voltage to a single node of the infinite grid will result in some
current flow into the grid, the puzzle is easily solved by simple symmetry
considerations. We assert (somewhat naively) that if we inject (say) four
Amperes of current into a given node, with no removal of current at any
finite point of the grid, the current will flow equally out through the four
resistors, so one Ampere will flow toward each of the four adjacent nodes.
This one Ampere must flow out through the three other lines emanating from
that adjacent node, as indicated in the left hand figure below.
The figure on the right shows the four nodes surrounding
the negative node, assuming we are extracting four Amperes from that node
(with no current injected at any finite node of the grid). Again, simple
symmetry dictates the distribution of currents indicated in the figure.
Adding the two current fields together, we see that the link between the
positive and negative nodes carries a total of 2 Amperes away from the
positive node, and the other three links emanating from the positive node
carry away a combined total of 1 + 1 + 1
-

)
= 2 Amperes. Thus the direct link carries
the same current as all the other paths, so the resistance of the direct link
equals the effective resistance of the entire grid excluding that link. The
direct link is in parallel with the remainder of the grid, so the combined
resistance is simply R/2.
This is an appealing argument, and it certainly gives the
right answer (as can be verified by other methods), but the premises are
somewhat questionable, and the reasoning involves some subtle issues that
need to be addressed before it can qualify as a rigorous proof. The
fundamental problem with the simple argument, as stated above, is that it

data.title: Chicken Eyeglasses
data.author: thomassmith65
data.article_summary: 鸡眼镜是一种小型眼镜，设计用于防止鸡之间的啄羽和同类相食行为。与遮眼片不同，鸡眼镜允许鸡向前看，同时遮挡特定视野以减少攻击性行为。早期20世纪在美国大规模生产和销售，通常由赛璐珞或铝制成，通过鼻孔固定。一些款式使用玫瑰色镜片，据信能掩盖血液颜色，从而减少啄伤，但效果存在争议。鸡眼镜曾是断喙术的替代方法，但因涉及组织穿刺，在某些国家被禁止。虽然已不再生产，但仍被作为收藏品，并在流行文化中出现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于鸡眼镜的用途、效果及背后的动物福利问题

不同观点：
• **hermitcrab**：认为应该以同理心和尊重对待有感知能力的生物，而不是将它们塞进人工环境中，喂抗生素、剪喙以及戴"可爱"的眼镜。这暗示了对现代畜牧业实践的批评。
• **WD-42**：幽默地指出文章没有附上鸡戴眼镜的图片是不完整的。
• **MaDeuce**：引用了哈佛商学院的一个案例研究，讨论了鸡眼镜的经济效益和市场推广策略，提供了一个商业视角。
• **wormius** 和 **gweinberg**：回忆了童年游戏中出现的鸡眼镜，带有怀旧色彩，并认为当时的一些发明如鸡眼镜并没有实际战略意义。
• **raptorraver**：提到现代工业蛋生产中使用红光来防止鸡群啄食，指出鸡眼镜可能是早期解决方案。
• **ortusdux**：分享了1970年代在研究实验室工作的经历，描述了用热铁烙曲喙以防止啄食的任务，认为眼镜方案更好。
• **Aardwolf**：质疑鸡眼镜是否已被替代，并指出今天仍有粉色塑料鸡眼镜出售，不确定是眼镜还是遮挡物。
• **thomassmith65**：通过ABC的播客了解了鸡眼镜，提供了额外信息来源。
• **kylecazar**：表示通过讨论学到了更多关于鸟类异常有害行为的知识。
• **FiddlerClamp**：回忆了1970年代的桌游《发明家》中出现的鸡眼镜，提供了图片链接。
• **ErigmolCt**：认为鸡眼镜是"寻找问题的解决方案"的典型例子，但也反映了前工业化时代的动物福利实践，具有历史趣味。
• **tomcam**：描述了自家养鸡的经验，指出鸡之间的攻击性行为，包括啄食顺序，并提到公鸡的攻击性需要隔离保护母鸡。

补充讨论：
• **WastedCucumber**：质疑鸡眼镜如何帮助防止啄食，认为文章没有清晰解释其保护机制。
• **miohtama**：提出鸡的行为问题是否源于过度拥挤的饲养环境，暗示了饲养密度可能是啄食问题的根本原因。

争议焦点：
• 鸡眼镜的实际效果和必要性受到质疑，特别是在现代畜牧业中是否有更人道的替代方案。
• 讨论中对鸡眼镜的幽默和怀旧态度与对其背后动物福利问题的严肃关注形成了对比。

44244675.article_content:
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Small eyeglasses made for chickens
1911 newspaper story on chicken eyeglasses from the
Spirit Lake Beacon
(Iowa)
[
1
]
Chicken eyeglasses
, also known as
chicken specs
,
chicken goggles
, generically as
pick guards
, and under other names,
[
2
]
were small
eyeglasses
made for
chickens
intended to prevent
feather pecking
and
cannibalism
. They differ from
blinders
in that they allow the bird to see forward, whereas blinders do not. One variety used
rose-colored
lenses, as the coloring was thought to prevent a chicken wearing them from recognizing blood on other chickens, which may increase the tendency for
abnormal injurious behavior
. They were
mass-produced
and sold throughout the United States as early as the beginning of the 20th century.
[
3
]
[
4
]
Description and purpose
[
edit
]
Chicken eyeglasses were often made from celluloid or aluminum
[
5
]
and typically consisted of "two oval panels that fit over the upper beak of the chicken. A pin is put through the nostril to hold the oval pieces in place."
[
2
]
Different designs were produced that attached to the chicken's head in different ways. Some were held in place by a strap,
[
3
]
some by small hooks into the
nares
(nostrils) and some by piercing the bone
septum
between the nostrils with a
cotter pin
.
[
6
]
Due to the piercing of tissue, this last type of design is illegal in some countries.
[fn. 1]
Some versions of the devices had semi- or fully transparent lenses, whereas others were tinted, often red- or rose-colored. Other designs were
blinders
, which are opaque and prevent entirely forward vision.
[
2
]
[
7
]
The intended purposes of chicken eyeglasses were to prevent aggressive pecking, cannibalism, and feather pecking.
Chicken eyeglasses are an alternative to
beak trimming
, which removes approximately one-third of the beak by a cold or heated blade or an infrared beam, usually when chicks are one day old. Beak trimming is often effective in reducing pecking injuries but causes pain and significantly affects chicken welfare.
[
7
]
[
8
]
[
9
]
[
10
]
[
11
]
Red-tinted lenses
[
edit
]
Red-tinted lenses were considered effective in reducing internecine pecking because they disguise the color of blood.
[
7
]
As summed up in a 1953 article in Indiana's
National Road Traveler
newspaper, "The deep rose-colored plastic lenses make it impossible for the cannibal [chicken] to see blood on the other chickens, although permitting it to see the grain on the ground."
[
12
]
Elmer Haas of the National Band & Tag Company, a major producer of rose-colored chicken eyeglasses, whose grandfather had devised wireframes for chickens in 1902,
[
13
]
indicated that he believed the purported blood-masking effect of the rose coloring was a myth: "the firm added the rose-colored glasses because it indulged the chicken owners ... [c]hickens are color blind".
[
13
]
(In fact, chickens, like other birds, have good
color vision
.
[
14
]
)  The firm had added the rose-colored feature to its glasses in 1939 under the brand name "Anti-Pix."
[
15
]
This variety of eyeglasses was more complicated than others because the red lenses were fixed to a hinge at the top of the frame. As the hen lowered its head to feed, the lens swung out, giving it an unobstructed view of the ground. When the hen raised her head, as she would during aggression, the lens would swing down giving the hen a red-tinted perception of the environment.
[
16
]
Rose-colored
contact lenses
, rather than eyeglasses, have also been proposed to reduce cannibalism in chickens.
[
17
]
History
[
edit
]
Detail from a 1903 patent filed by Andrew Jackson Jr.
A form of chicken eyeglasses was first patented in 1903 by Andrew Jackson Jr. of
Munich
,
Tennessee
, as an "Eye-protector for chickens."
[
18
]
In the U.S., they were available through the mail order company
Sears-Roebuck
or chicken feed stores for a few cents.
[
19
]
The eyeglasses are no longer produced by the National Band & Tag Company, but are sought as
collector's items
.
[
6
]
Using chicken eyeglasses was still practiced in 1973, evidenced by Illinois'
The Hawk-Eye
newspaper that a farmer had 8,000 chickens fitted with the rose-colored variety.
[
20
]
One inventor of a form of the glasses proposed legislation in
Kansas
to require
all
chickens in the state to be fitted with glasses, but his campaign was unsuccessful.
[
21
]
In popular culture
[
edit
]
On January 16, 1955, Sam Nadler of the National Farm Equipment Company of Brooklyn appeared on
CBS
' popular primetime television show,
What's My Line?
[
22
]
The show was in the format of a
guessing game
, in which a panel attempted to determine the line (occupation) of contestants.
[
23
]
Show officials listed Mr. Nadler's occupation for the audience as "sells 'eyeglasses' for chickens". After the panel was unsuccessful in guessing his occupation,  Mr. Nadler's identity was revealed, and he stated that his company sold 2–3 million pairs of chicken eyeglasses annually.
