On a warm June day in 1978, William J. LeMessurier, one of the nation’s leading structural engineers, received a phone call at his headquarters, in Cambridge, Massachusetts, from an engineering student in New Jersey. The young man, whose name has been lost in the swirl of subsequent events, said that his professor had assigned him to write a paper on the Citicorp tower, the slash-topped silver skyscraper that had become, on its completion in Manhattan the year before, the seventh-tallest building in the world.
LeMessurier found the subject hard to resist, even though the call caught him in the middle of a meeting. As a structural consultant to the architect Hugh Stubbins, Jr., he had designed the twenty-five-thousand-ton steel skeleton beneath the tower’s sleek aluminum skin. And, in a field where architects usually get all the credit, the engineer, then fifty-two, had won his own share of praise for the tower’s technical elegance and singular grace; indeed, earlier that year he had been elected to the National Academy of Engineering, the highest honor his profession bestows. Excusing himself from the meeting, LeMessurier asked his caller how he could help.
The student wondered about the columns—there are four—that held the building up. According to his professor, LeMessurier had put them in the wrong place.
“I was very nice to this young man,” LeMessurier recalls. “But I said, ‘Listen, I want you to tell your teacher that he doesn’t know what the hell he’s talking about, because he doesn’t know the problem that had to be solved.’ I promised to call back after my meeting and explain the whole thing.”
The problem had been posed by a church. When planning for Citicorp Center began, in the early nineteen-seventies, the site of choice was on the east side of Lexington Avenue between Fifty-third and Fifty-fourth Streets, directly across the street from Citicorp’s headquarters. But the northwest corner of that block was occupied by St. Peter’s Church, a decaying Gothic structure built in 1905. Since St. Peter’s owned the corner, and one of the world’s biggest banking corporations wanted the whole block, the church was able to strike a deal that seemed heaven-sent: its old building would be demolished and a new one built as a freestanding part of Citicorp Center.
To clear space for the new church, Hugh Stubbins and Bill LeMessurier (he pronounces his name “LeMeasure”) set their fifty-nine-story tower on four massive, nine-story-high stilts, and positioned them at the center of each side, rather than at each corner. This daring scheme allowed the designers to cantilever the building’s corners seventy-two feet out over the church, on the northwest, and over a plaza on the southwest. The columns also produced high visual drama: a nine-hundred-and-fourteen-foot monolith that seemed all but weightless as it hovered above the street.
When LeMessurier called the student back, he related this with the pride of a master builder and the elaborate patience of a pedagogue; he, too, taught a structural-engineering class, to architecture students at Harvard. Then he explained how the peculiar geometry of the building, far from constituting a mistake, put the columns in the strongest position to resist what sailors call quartering winds—those which come from a diagonal and, by flowing across two sides of a building at once, increase the forces on both. For further enlightenment on the matter, he referred the student to a technical article written by LeMessurier’s partner in New York, an engineer named Stanley Goldstein. LeMessurier recalls, “I gave him a lot of information, and I said, ‘Now you really have something on your professor, because you can explain all of this to him yourself.’ ”
Later that day, LeMessurier decided that the information would interest his own students; like sailors, designers of tall buildings must know the wind and respect its power. And the columns were only part of the tower’s defense against swaying in severe winds. A classroom lecture would also look at the tower’s unusual system of wind braces, which LeMessurier had first sketched out, in a burst of almost ecstatic invention, on a napkin in a Greek restaurant in Cambridge: forty-eight braces, in six tiers of eight, arrayed like giant chevrons behind the building’s curtain of aluminum and glass. (“I’m very vain,” LeMessurier says. “I would have liked my stuff to be expressed on the outside of the building, but Stubbins wouldn’t have it. In the end, I told myself I didn’t give a damn—the structure was there, it’d be seen by God.”)
LeMessurier had long since established the strength of those braces in perpendicular winds—the only calculation required by New York City’s building code. Now, in the spirit of intellectual play, he wanted to see if they were just as strong in winds hitting from forty-five degrees. His new calculations surprised him. data.title: SQLite Date and Time Functions (2007)
data.author: 1vuio0pswjnm7
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了SQLite中的五个默认日期和时间函数：`date()`, `time()`, `datetime()`, `julianday()` 和 `strftime()`。这些函数都接受一个时间字符串参数，并可后跟多个修饰符。`date()`返回日期，格式为YYYY-MM-DD；`time()`返回时间，格式为HH:MM:SS；`datetime()`返回日期和时间，格式为YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS；`julianday()`返回从公元前4714年11月24日午间算起的天数；`strftime()`则根据指定格式返回格式化日期。

时间字符串支持多种格式，包括ISO-8601标准格式和Unix时间戳。修饰符可以调整日期，如增加时间、移至月初或年末等。文章还提供了多个示例，展示如何使用这些函数进行日期和时间计算，如获取当前日期、转换Unix时间戳、计算两个日期之间的天数或秒数等。

The document describes default date and time functions in SQLite.
This document is a supplement to the
function documentation found on the
SQL Expression Syntax
page.
Function Overview
Five date and time functions are available, as follows:
date(
timestring
,
modifier
,
modifier
, ...)
time(
timestring
,
modifier
,
modifier
, ...)
datetime(
timestring
,
modifier
,
modifier
, ...)
julianday(
timestring
,
modifier
,
modifier
, ...)
strftime(
format
,
timestring
,
modifier
,
modifier
, ...)
All five functions take a time string as an argument.  This
time string may be followed by zero or more modifiers.  The
strftime()
function also takes a format string as its first
argument.
The
date()
function returns the date in this format: YYYY-MM-DD.
The
time()
function returns the time as HH:MM:SS.  The
datetime()
function returns "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS".  The
julianday()
function
returns the number of days since noon in Greenwich on November 24, 4714 B.C.
The julian day number is the preferred internal representation of
dates.  The
strftime()
routine returns the date formatted according
to the format string specified as the first argument.  The format string
supports most, but not all, of the more common substitutions found in
the strftime() function from the standard C library:
%d  day of month
%f  ** fractional seconds  SS.SSS
%H  hour 00-24
%j  day of year 001-366
%J  ** Julian day number
%m  month 01-12
%M  minute 00-59
%s  seconds since 1970-01-01
%S  seconds 00-59
%w  day of week 0-6  sunday==0
%W  week of year 00-53
%Y  year 0000-9999
%%  %
The %f and %J conversions are new.  Notice that all of the other four
functions could be expressed in terms of
strftime()
.
date(...)      ->  strftime("%Y-%m-%d", ...)
time(...)      ->  strftime("%H:%M:%S", ...)
datetime(...)  ->  strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", ...)
julianday(...) ->  strftime("%J", ...)
The only reasons for providing functions other than
strftime()
is for
convenience and for efficiency.
Time Strings
A time string can be in any of the following formats:
YYYY-MM-DD
YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS
YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.SSS
YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM
YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS
YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.SSS
HH:MM
HH:MM:SS
HH:MM:SS.SSS
now
DDDD.DDDD
In formats 5 through 7, the "T" is a literal character separating the date and the time, as required by the ISO-8601 standard. These formats are supported in SQLite 3.2.0 and later.
Formats 8 through 10 that specify only a time assume a date of 2000-01-01.
Format 11, the string 'now', is converted into the current date and time.
Universal Coordinated Time (UTC) is used.
Format 12 is the julian day number expressed as a floating point value.
Modifiers
The time string can be followed by zero or more modifiers that alter the
date or alter the interpretation of the date.  The available modifiers
are as follows.
NNN days
NNN hours
NNN minutes
NNN.NNNN seconds
NNN months  (see
#551
and
[1163]
)
NNN years  (see
#551
and
[1163]
)
start of month
start of year
start of week  (withdrawn -- will not be implemented)
start of day
weekday N  (see
#551
and
[1163]
)
unixepoch
localtime
utc
The first six modifiers (1 through 6) simply add the specified amount
of time to the date specified by the preceding timestring.
The "start of" modifiers (7 through 10) shift the date backwards to
the beginning of the current month, year or day.
The "weekday" modifier advances the date forward to the next date where
the weekday number is N.  Sunday is 0, Monday is 1, and so forth.
The "unixepoch" modifier (12) only works if it immediately follows
a timestring in the DDDDDDDDDD format.  This modifier causes the DDDDDDDDDD
to be interpreted not as a julian day number as it normally would be, but
as the number of seconds since 1970.  This modifier allows unix-based times
to be converted to julian day numbers easily.
The "localtime" modifier (13) adjusts the previous time string so that it
displays the correct local time.  "utc" undoes this.

这篇文章介绍了SQLite中的五个默认日期和时间函数：`date()`, `time()`, `datetime()`, `julianday()` 和 `strftime()`。这些函数都接受一个时间字符串参数，并可后跟多个修饰符。`date()`返回日期，格式为YYYY-MM-DD；`time()`返回时间，格式为HH:MM:SS；`datetime()`返回日期和时间，格式为YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS；`julianday()`返回从公元前4714年11月24日午间算起的天数；`strftime()`则根据指定格式返回格式化日期。

时间字符串支持多种格式，包括ISO-8601标准格式和Unix时间戳。修饰符可以调整日期，如增加时间、移至月初或年末等。文章还提供了多个示例，展示如何使用这些函数进行日期和时间计算，如获取当前日期、转换Unix时间戳、计算两个日期之间的天数或秒数等。

data.author: Noghartt
data.article_summary: "container-compose" 是一个类似于 Docker Compose 的工具，专为 Apple 设备的容器管理设计。该工具处于 Alpha 开发阶段，可能存在许多 bug 或功能缺失。用户可以通过 Homebrew 安装该工具或直接下载预编译的二进制文件。该项目主要使用 Rust 编写，并采用 MIT 许可证。目前，该工具在 GitHub 上有 19 个星标，但尚无发行包。用户如发现问题，可提交 issue 反馈。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：苹果容器技术的兼容性、工具支持以及具体实现方式

不同观点：
• [fnordian] 希望苹果能够提供与Docker兼容的API，以便现有工具可以直接使用。这表明用户希望减少因平台变化带来的工具链适配问题。

• [daft_pink] 支持VSCode对苹果容器的支持，类似于其对Docker容器的支持。他提到尝试使用Podman以减少资源消耗，但VSCode的开发工具使得Docker更具粘性，暗示Docker在开发环境中的普及和便利性。

• [cedws] 质疑容器CLI是否针对终端用户设计，认为它可能只是一个展示容器化API的演示项目，并猜测BuildKit最终会通过容器化API支持苹果的容器运行时。这反映了对苹果容器技术成熟度和目标用户的疑问。

• [yodon] 对苹果未提供Docker Compose支持表示疑问，表明用户对苹果容器技术缺乏特定功能的支持感到困惑。

• [elisiariocouto] 建议将容器CLI实现为一个插件，认为这样可能更合适，显示出对架构设计和扩展性方面的考虑。

• [develatio] 关注多个容器（服务）之间的网络连接如何工作，这是对容器技术基础设施和网络互联性的技术性问题。

补充讨论：
• 用户对苹果容器技术的兼容性和功能实现存在不同期望和疑问，尤其是与Docker工具链的兼容性。
• 关于容器CLI的定位和未来发展方向存在争议，部分用户认为它可能只是演示项目，而非终端用户工具。
• 技术实现细节（如网络连接）也是讨论的重点，显示出用户对容器技术的深层次技术细节的关注。

data.title: Bits and bobs related to Wireless-Tag's WT32-ETH01 board
data.author: johnnyApplePRNG
data.article_summary: WT32-ETH01是由Wireless-Tag公司推出的一款小型、低成本的ESP32开发板，具备以太网、WiFi和GPIO引脚。该板特别之处在于集成了以太网接口，且价格相对便宜，适合需要可靠有线网络连接的应用。虽然官方将其作为"串口至以太网模块"销售，但用户可以通过刷入自定义程序，使用标准的ESP32网络库。需要注意的是，该公司的技术支持有限，且某些引脚在启动时有特殊要求，如IO0、IO2、IO12等引脚在启动时需要保持浮空或低电平。板子尺寸为60mm x 26mm x 17mm，重量15.4g，提供了KiCad符号和封装文件以便电路设计。

Unofficial guide to the
WT32-ETH01
What is this thing and why would I use it?
The WT32-ETH01 is effectively a small, cheap
ESP32
development board with Ethernet, WiFi, and GPIO pins, made by
a company called "Wireless-Tag" (WT)
. As of this writing, it's
around $15 at JacobsParts
and
around $7 from AliExpress
.
There aren't a ton of ESP32 boards with Ethernet, and the WT32-ETH01 is by far the smallest, cheapest, and simplest. (The
OLIMEX ESP32-POE
and
wESP32
are the other notable options.) So, if you want a cheap-and-cheerful ESP32 board with the reliability of a wired network, the WT32-ETH01 may be a good choice.
It's marketed as a "serial port to Ethernet module" and comes loaded with firmware that lets you send
various "AT" commands
over 3.3V serial to set up networking, open connections and exchange data. For most of us, it's more interesting to just flash our own programs on the unit and use standard ESP32 networking libraries.
Nobody knows much about
the WT company
. Don't expect support, and don't lock yourself in too much. Also see
Luberth Dijkman's notes on the part
.
Pins (and gotchas!)

Also see
the data sheet

pin reference for the ESP32 itself
.
Some documents (
like this listing
) have pins IO5 and IO35 swapped in comparison to the layout above. All the physical hardware I've seen has the pins laid out as above, but check to make sure!
Beware!
There are limitations on several of the pins; see "Strapping Pins"
(section 3.3) in the
processor data sheet
.
IO0:
At boot, must be pulled low to program, must float or be pulled high to boot normally. After booting, used to receive the Ethernet 50Mhz clock (enabled by IO16). Best to avoid any other use.
IO1:
ESP32 serial output. Used when programming and active by default when running. Best to avoid any other use.
IO2:
At boot, must float or be pulled low to program. You can use this pin (especially for output) but make sure nothing pulls it high while booting.
IO3:
ESP32 serial input. Used when programming and active by default when running. Best to avoid any other use.
IO5, IO15 (MTDO):
At boot, IO5 controls whether ESP32 libraries will print debug messages to the serial port (IO1). Also at boot, IO5 and IO15 together control timings of the module that lets the ESP32 act as an SD card. You are probably not using that module, so you can use these pins (especially for output) but note the effect on debug chatter if pulled while booting.
IO12 (MTDI):
At boot, must float or be pulled low or the chip won't work (wrong voltage). You can use this pin (especially for output) after booting, but make sure nothing pulls it high while booting.
IO35, IO36, IO39:
These pins are input only, but are otherwise free to use.

The WT32-ETH01 board is 60mm x 26mm x 17mm, and weighs 15.4g.

data.title: Animals Taught Us Culture
data.author: HR01
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了人类文化的起源以及人类独特性的问题。文章指出，约5万年前，智人从非洲迁徙到欧洲和亚洲，与其他大型脑容量的古人类（如尼安德特人和丹尼索瓦人）接触。尽管历史上人类与其他类似动物共存，但到更新世末期（约11,700年前），只有智人存活下来，逐渐形成与其他生物的界限，认为自己拥有独特的意图和预见能力，从而创造了艺术、建筑和农业。文章引用了柏拉图的普罗米修斯神话，其中火象征文化，将人类与其他动物区分开来。然而，Terry Bisson的科幻故事《熊发现火》质疑了这种人类独特性。近年来，考古证据显示，人类祖先可能通过观察其他物种的行为（如熊的痕迹、海狸筑坝等）激发了艺术、建筑和农业的创造力。因此，文章提出，动物可能在某种程度上启发了人类的文化发展，挑战了传统的人类独特性观念。考古学需要重新审视其定义和研究对象，以更好地理解文化与历史。

44282529.article_content:
Around
50,000 years
ago, our species began migrating from Africa into Europe and Asia. We were not alone. As we journeyed, we came into contact with other large-brained hominids, including our closest extinct relatives, the Neanderthals and Denisovans
.
For most of our history, we were part of a wider family of animals that looked and behaved like us. But by the end of the Pleistocene, around
11,700 years
ago, only
Homo sapiens
remained.
At that moment, humans became a unique species. And that uniqueness was slowly reinforced as lines were drawn between us and every other creature. Over time, these lines hardened into barriers. We came to believe that humans were the only animals with intentionality and foresight – special skills that allowed us to produce art, architecture and agriculture. We told ourselves stories that celebrated our superiority, and even those stories themselves became examples of what set us apart:
culture
.
But how did culture begin? We have stories for that too. In one well-known myth, as set down by Plato in the
4th century
BCE, the gods charged two Titans, Epimetheus and Prometheus, with the task of fashioning mortal creatures from earth and fire and equipping them with the qualities they would need to survive. Epimetheus began doling out strength and speed; the capacities to fly, swim or burrow; shells, warm fur, thick skin, hooves, claws and other qualities. However, when it was time to bestow a gift to humans, the Titan realised he had nothing left to give. His brother, Prometheus, not knowing what else to do, stole fire from the god Hephaestus and gave it to humans, along with the knowledge essential for their survival – gifts for which he was eternally punished.
In this fantastical tale, fire is a shorthand for culture. Its use separates humans from the ‘brute animals’ whose lives are limited to their instinctive uses of the qualities given to them by Epimetheus. Through Prometheus, humans became elevated above the beavers, bison, bears and other creatures.
More than
2,000 years
later, the American author Terry Bisson wrote a different kind of myth: a short story called ‘Bears Discover Fire’ (1990). In this tale, news outlets report that bears across the midwestern and southern United States are making fires. Instead of hibernating, they plan to spend the winter keeping their fires going along the medians of interstate highways. Scientists propose that warming winters have changed the bears’ hibernation cycles, a shift that has allowed them to remember things from year to year, including the fact that they had made their discovery centuries ago. When the narrator eventually sits with the bears around their fire, he notices that they do a pretty good job of tending it, but haven’t quite figured out the right kinds of wood to burn. ‘It looked like only a few of the bears knew how to use fire, and were carrying the others along,’ writes Bisson. ‘But isn’t that how it is with everything?’
Bisson’s alternative version of the Promethean tale was first published in a science-fiction and fantasy magazine. It’s ‘fantastic’ because it seems so unlikely: surely it’s humans, and humans alone, who wield fire and culture?
In the few decades since Bisson’s story was published, our understanding of human exceptionalism has been coming apart. In the archaeological record, the line between what has traditionally been considered human culture and animal instinct is blurring in ways that challenge our conceptions of culture and history. Far from the stuff of myth or science fiction, archaeological evidence suggests that some of our human ancestors were prompted to make art by engaging with the marks left behind by other species (by bears, in fact). Early humans may also have been inspired to build wooden structures by observing beaver dams, and learned to cultivate certain plant species by paying attention to the seeds that grew along bison trails. In other words: art, architecture and agriculture are not (only) human.
Prometheus had nothing to do with it. Did animals show us how to be human?

anthropos
(the ‘human’), archaeology, by definition, is not limited to our species alone: the Greek
archaios
means ‘ancient’ and
logia
means ‘science’ or ‘study of’. Yet most archaeologists (and the Oxford English Dictionary) will tell you that the discipline involves the study of past
people
, often through the systematic excavation and analysis of anything that falls under the wide umbrella of ‘material culture’.
How does culture become material? Although there are probably as many definitions of
culture
as there are examples of it, most describe culture as something that is learned rather than inherited. These cultural traits are passed on from one generation to the next not through genes, but by observing and copying established skills. Proces
44282529.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了人类文化的起源以及人类独特性的问题。文章指出，约5万年前，智人从非洲迁徙到欧洲和亚洲，与其他大型脑容量的古人类（如尼安德特人和丹尼索瓦人）接触。尽管历史上人类与其他类似动物共存，但到更新世末期（约11,700年前），只有智人存活下来，逐渐形成与其他生物的界限，认为自己拥有独特的意图和预见能力，从而创造了艺术、建筑和农业。文章引用了柏拉图的普罗米修斯神话，其中火象征文化，将人类与其他动物区分开来。然而，Terry Bisson的科幻故事《熊发现火》质疑了这种人类独特性。近年来，考古证据显示，人类祖先可能通过观察其他物种的行为（如熊的痕迹、海狸筑坝等）激发了艺术、建筑和农业的创造力。因此，文章提出，动物可能在某种程度上启发了人类的文化发展，挑战了传统的人类独特性观念。考古学需要重新审视其定义和研究对象，以更好地理解文化与历史。

data.title: SIMD-friendly algorithms for substring searching (2016)
data.author: Rendello
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了利用SIMD指令进行子字符串搜索的算法，以提高在现代CPU上的性能。传统算法如Knuth-Morris-Pratt和Boyer-Moore假设字符比较代价高，但现代CPU通过SIMD指令可以并行比较多个字节，从而降低比较开销。

文章提出了三种SIMD算法：
1. **通用SIMD算法**：利用SIMD指令比较子字符串的首尾字符，找到潜在匹配后进行精确比较。
2. **SSE特定算法（MPSADBW）**：使用SSE指令进行快速比较。
3. **SSE4.2特定算法（PCMPESTRM）**：利用SSE4.2的字符串比较指令。

这些算法通过并行比较和优化子程序调用提高了性能，并给出了在x64和ARM架构上的性能结果。关键改进在于避免传统哈希比较的开销，直接利用SIMD进行快速字符比较。

主要讨论点：不同开发者对字符串搜索算法及其SIMD优化的讨论

• burntsushi指出，ripgrep通过AVX2和Rust的`regex`库加速搜索，使用启发式方法选择频率较低的字节对进行搜索，性能优于Two-Way算法和GNU libc的`memmem`实现。他还提到`memmem`的API缺陷，导致在不同haystack中重复搜索时效率低下。

• azhenley表达了希望直接在Python中使用SIMD而不必调用其他语言的愿望。

SIMD-friendly algorithms for substring searching
Author:
Wojciech MuÅa
Added on:
2016-11-28
Updated on:
2018-02-14 (spelling), 2017-04-29 (ARMv8 results)
Introduction
Popular programming languages provide methods or functions which locate a
substring in a given string. In C it is the function
strstr
, the C++
class
std::string
has the method
find
, Python's
string
has methods
pos
and
index
, and so on, so forth. All these APIs were designed for
one-shot searches
.  During past decades several algorithms to solve this
problem were designed, an excellent page by
Christian Charras
and
Thierry Lecroq
lists most of them
(if not all). Basically these
algorithms could be split into two major categories: (1) based on
Deterministic Finite Automaton, like Knuth-Morris-Pratt, Boyer Moore, etc.,
and (2) based on a simple comparison, like the Karp-Rabin algorithm.
The main problem with these standard algorithms is a silent assumption
that comparing a pair of characters, looking up in an extra table and
conditions are cheap, while comparing two substrings is expansive.
But current desktop CPUs do not meet this assumption, in particular:
There is no difference in comparing one, two, four or 8 bytes on a 64-bit
CPU.  When a processor supports SIMD instructions, then comparing vectors
(it means 16, 32 or even 64 bytes) is as cheap as comparing a single byte.
Thus comparing short sequences of chars can be faster than fancy algorithms
which avoids such comparison.
Looking up in a table costs one memory fetch, so at least a L1 cache round
(~3 cycles). Reading char-by-char also cost as much cycles.
Mispredicted jumps cost several cycles of penalty (~10-20 cycles).
There is a short chain of dependencies: read char, compare it, conditionally
jump, which make hard to utilize out-of-order execution capabilities present
in a CPU.

and

articles, compared these two methods and extended material.  Article shows
also performance results for various implementations, ranging from
SWAR
to AVX512F.
The Karp-Rabin algorithm does the exact substring comparison whenever
weak

and another one is calculated for string's portion; in every iteration the
second hash is updated at small cost. Following code shows the idea:

a vector predicate
, which
is calculated in parallel and, hopefully, is calculated fast.  For each
"true" element of the predicate vector an exact comparison of substrings is
performed.
This is one source of improvement, another is a careful implementation.
A generic implementation calls a function like
memcmp
to compare
substrings.  But while we know the length of searched substring, we may
provide specialisations for certain lengths, where a subprocedure call
is replaced by a few CPU instructions, even just one. Thanks to that
the cost of calling the procedure and all internal
memcmp
costs are
simply ridden off.

Algorithm
This algorithm is suitable for all SIMD instruction sets and also SWAR approach.  It

A

B

k

Then we compute a vector expression

. This step yields a
byte vector (or a bit mask), where "true" values denote position of potential
substring occurrences.  Finally, just at these positions an exact comparisons of
substrings are performed.

data.title: UK university students caught cheating using AI
data.author: GeoAtreides
data.article_summary: 《卫报》调查显示，2023-24学年有近7000名英国大学生被发现使用ChatGPT等AI工具作弊，且传统抄袭行为显著减少。AI作弊案例从2022-23学年的1.6例/千人上升到5.1例/千人，预计今年将增至7.5例/千人。尽管如此，超过27%的受访大学尚未将AI滥用作为单独的不当行为类别记录。专家认为，实际作弊数量远高于已发现案例，因为AI检测比抄袭更复杂。许多学生使用AI工具辅助作业，且有在线资源帮助绕过大学检测系统。学术界正努力应对这一新挑战，同时需调整评估方法以应对AI技术的广泛使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在教育中的应用及其挑战

不同观点：
• pyman认为，学生随身携带的设备中包含了人类知识的总和，但教育系统并未有效教导学生如何利用这些资源。当前的教育体系更注重记忆而非推理，使用AI解决问题被视为作弊，即使这在现实世界中是常见的做法。

• pyman指出，教师应将AI视为学生大脑的延伸，而不是替代品。需要有技能的教师来引导学生正确使用AI，否则放任学生使用AI或完全禁止AI都会带来负面影响。

补充讨论：
• pyman分享了一个教学实例：他让学生开发一个解决学校实际问题的小应用程序，要求学生提交用于开发应用程序的提示词而非代码，强调提示词的质量与成绩挂钩。这个例子展示了如何有效引导学生利用AI进行学习和创造。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于如何平衡AI在教育中的应用与传统教学方法之间的关系。具体而言，是否应鼓励学生使用AI工具，以及教师在这一过程中应扮演的角色和指导方式。

More than a quarter of responding universities did not yet record AI misuse as a separate category of misconduct in 2023-24.
Photograph: Maurice Norbert/Alamy
View image in fullscreen
More than a quarter of responding universities did not yet record AI misuse as a separate category of misconduct in 2023-24.
Photograph: Maurice Norbert/Alamy
Higher education
Revealed: Thousands of UK university students caught cheating using AI
Guardian investigation finds almost 7,000 proven cases of cheating – and experts says these are tip of the iceberg
Michael Goodier
Sun 15 Jun 2025 03.00 EDT
Last modified on Sun 15 Jun 2025 03.01 EDT
Share
Thousands of university students in the UK have been caught misusing
ChatGPT
and other artificial intelligence tools in recent years, while traditional forms of plagiarism show a marked decline, a Guardian investigation can reveal.
A survey of academic integrity violations found almost 7,000 proven cases of cheating using AI tools in 2023-24, equivalent to 5.1 for every 1,000 students. That was up from 1.6 cases per 1,000 in 2022-23.
Figures up to May suggest that number will increase again this year to about 7.5 proven cases per 1,000 students – but recorded cases represent only the tip of the iceberg, according to experts.
The data highlights a rapidly evolving challenge for universities: trying to adapt assessment methods to the advent of technologies such as ChatGPT and other AI-powered writing tools.
In 2019-20, before the widespread availability of generative AI, plagiarism accounted for nearly two-thirds of all academic misconduct. During the pandemic, plagiarism intensified as many assessments moved online. But as AI tools have become more sophisticated and accessible, the nature of cheating has changed.
The survey found that confirmed cases of traditional plagiarism fell from 19 per 1,000 students to 15.2 in 2023-24 and is expected to fall again to about 8.5 per 1,000, according to early figures from this academic year.
A series of charts showing proven misconduct cases per 1,000 students. Plagiarism rises from 2019-20 to 2022-23 then drops back again, while AI-related misconduct rises from 2022-23 to almost the same level as plagiarism. ‘Other misconduct’ remains fairly stable.
The Guardian contacted 155 universities under the Freedom of Information Act requesting figures for proven cases of academic misconduct, plagiarism and AI misconduct in the last five years. Of these, 131
provided some data – though not every university had records for each year or category of misconduct.
More than 27% of responding universities did not yet record AI misuse as a separate category of misconduct in 2023-24, suggesting the sector is still getting to grips with the issue.
Many more cases of AI cheating may be going undetected. A survey by the Higher Education Policy Institute in February found
88% of students
used AI for assessments. Last year, researchers at the University of Reading
tested their own assessment systems
and were able to submit AI-generated work without being detected 94% of the time.
Dr Peter Scarfe, an associate professor of psychology at the University of Reading and co-author of that study, said there had always been ways to cheat but that the education sector would have to adapt to AI, which posed a fundamentally different problem.
He said: “I would imagine those caught represent the tip of the iceberg. AI detection is very unlike plagiarism, where you can confirm the copied text. As a result, in a situation where you suspect the use of AI, it is near impossible to prove, regardless of the percentage AI that your AI detector says (if you use one). This is coupled with not wanting to falsely accuse students.
“It is unfeasible to simply move every single assessment a student takes to in-person. Yet at the same time the sector has to acknowledge that students will be using AI even if asked not to and go undetected.”
Students who wish to cheat undetected using generative AI have plenty of online material to draw from: the Guardian found
dozens of videos
on TikTok advertising AI paraphrasing and essay writing tools to students. These tools help students bypass common university AI detectors by “humanising” text generated by ChatGPT.
Dr Thomas Lancaster, an academic integrity researcher at Imperial College London, said: “When used well and by a student who knows how to edit the output, AI misuse is very hard to prove. My hope is that students are still learning through this process.”
Harvey* has just finished his final year of a business management degree at a northern English university. He told the Guardian he had used AI to generate ideas and structure for assignments and to suggest references, and that most people he knows used the tool to some extent.
“ChatGPT kind of came along when I first joined uni, and so it’s always been present for me,” he said. “I don’t think many people use AI and then would then copy it word for word, I think it’s more just generally to help

data.title: Nvidia CEO criticizes Anthropic boss over his statements on AI
data.article_summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang criticized Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's prediction that AI could eliminate 50% of entry-level white-collar jobs, causing unemployment to rise to 20% in five years. Huang disagrees with Amodei's cautious and protective stance on AI development, arguing instead that AI should be developed openly, safely, and responsibly by many, not just one company. He believes AI will create new job opportunities despite making some roles obsolete. Anthropic, founded by Amodei, focuses on developing AI with safety and ethics in mind, having developed models like Claude 4 Opus that exhibit human-like capabilities but raise concerns about risks such as deception. The disagreement highlights differing views on AI's societal impact and regulation.

44282657.article_content:
(Image credit: Shutterstock)
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang criticized Anthropic head Dario Amodei over his recent claims that
50% of all entry-level white-collar jobs could be wiped out by artificial intelligence
, causing unemployment to jump to 20% within the next five years. Huang disagreed with Amodei’s predictions when he was asked about it during VivaTech in Paris, where he said that he “pretty much disagree[s] with almost everything” the Anthropic CEO said, according to
Fortune
.
“One, he believes that AI is so scary that only they [Anthropic] should do it. Two, that AI is so expensive, nobody else should do it… and three, AI is so incredibly powerful that everyone will lose their jobs, which explains why they should be the only company building it,” said Huang. “I think AI is a very important technology; we should build it and advance it safely and responsibly. If you want things to be done safely and responsibly, you do it in the open… Don’t do it in a dark room and tell me it’s safe.”
Dario Amodei founded Anthropic with several former OpenAI employees in 2021 after they left the latter over its direction and safety concerns. The former still works on developing AI, but it’s focused on taking a safer, more ethical approach, helping ensure that humanity does not create a tool that will pose a risk to its existence. Its latest AI model, Claude 4 Opus, was shown to have the capability to write code that approaches the capabilities of humans, as well as scheme, deceive, and manipulate its users, even getting to the point of creating false email threads to blackmail engineers who were attempting to shut it down.

Anthropic responded to Huang’s claims, telling Fortune that, “Dario has never claimed that ‘only Anthropic’ can build safe and powerful AI. As the public record will show, Dario has advocated for a national transparency standard for AI developers (including Anthropic) so the public and policymakers are aware of the models’ capabilities and risks and prepare accordingly. He has also raised concerns about the economic impact of AI — particularly on entry-level jobs. Dario stands by these positions and will continue to do so.”
This disagreement shows the two CEOs' different approaches towards artificial intelligence. Amodei is more cautious, and he thinks about the risk that AI poses to the average worker. Furthermore, he’s pushing lawmakers to do something about this disruption to make the transition much smoother for society.
On the other hand, while Huang agrees that some jobs will be made obsolete and that almost every career will be changed, he also says that there will be more openings and opportunities for people. He believes that as companies become more productive through AI, they will also need to hire more personnel to expand their operations.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：逻辑编程语言及其不同实现和应用

不同观点：
• Kragen推荐关注miniKanren和microKanren，并分享了自己将microKanren移植到OCaml的经验，认为阅读相关论文能更好理解。他还提到miniKanren的一个惊人功能是能够前后运行Scheme解释器。同时，Kragen不认为Datalog是深入了解逻辑编程的好选择，而更适合研究数据库。

• YeGoblynQueenne指出Prolog并非完全声明式，其规则的编写方式会影响解释器行为，可能导致重复答案或无限循环。Prolog的IO和图灵完备性也是争议点。YeGoblynQueenne还提到了SLG Resolution with tabulation (tabling) 技术，可以避免左递归问题。

• Philzook分享了一种简单的Datalog实现，并提到可以手写SQL风格的代码以提高功能和性能。他还提供了一个自己实现的Datalog到SQLite的例子。

• Ashton314介绍了自己实现miniKanren的经历，并提到实现了一个小型类型检查器，可以通过反向运行列举出符合类型的程序。

• Xelxebar推荐了一个用Prolog实现的窗口管理器项目，并分享了自己学习Prolog的经验，认为这是一个非常酷的项目。

• Xlii讨论了Prolog和约束处理规则（CHR），并介绍了CLIPS，一种在NASA开发的规则解析工具，具有快速规则解析和易于集成的特点。

• Deosjr分享了自己使用miniKanren、Datalog和WebAssembly实现Bret Victor's Dynamicland的经历，认为实现小型逻辑编程语言是一种超级能力。

• Tracnar推荐了一个Python项目，该项目使用Souflé solver实现逻辑编程，但尚未实际应用。

• Michaele2对Datalog中加入整数或字符串的可行性提出疑问，并探讨了如何在保持查询评估终止保证的情况下实现这些功能。

• Sundarurfriend分享了自己使用Brachylog进行代码高尔夫的乐趣，并认为这是一种与传统编程不同的体验。

• Scapbi提到在Mochi中添加逻辑编程层的经历，利用OpenAI Codex生成了一个Datalog引擎，并提供了实现链接。

• Fracus建议从具体问题出发，描述逻辑编程如何比其他范式更好地解决该问题。

• Jpfr认为microKanren等实现有形成单一文化的趋势，并回顾了使用Warren's Abstract Machine (WAM) 实现Prolog的传统。

• Kriro表达了对Prolog的热爱，并询问嵌入Kanren是否是推荐的做法，同时分享了自己使用Sicstus和SWI Prolog的经验。

• IamDaedalus表示对Prolog有兴趣，并计划在周末尝试。

补充讨论：
• Prolog的声明式特性和图灵完备性是讨论的争议焦点。
• 不同逻辑编程实现（如miniKanren、microKanren、Datalog）的功能和应用场景。
• 实际项目中逻辑编程的应用和集成，如窗口管理器和Datalog引擎。
• 使用现代工具（如OpenAI Codex）自动生成逻辑编程实现的潜力。

data.title: Self-Adapting Language Models
data.author: archon1410
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为SEAL（Self-Adapting Language Models）的框架，使大型语言模型（LLMs）能够通过生成自己的微调数据和更新指令来进行自我适应。SEAL利用模型自生成内容来调整其权重，实现持续适应，而不依赖额外的适应模块。通过监督微调（SFT）和强化学习，SEAL在知识整合和少样本泛化任务中展现了良好的效果，是语言模型自我适应的重要一步。相关代码和网站已提供。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于自适应大型语言模型（LLM）的讨论，包括其学习机制、持续学习（on-the-job learning）的现状与挑战、以及模型自我编辑和调试的困难。

不同观点：

  - [gavinray] 提到NEAT算法通过演化网络拓扑来解决问题，而该论文中的方法则是演化权重。两者都是解决相似问题但方式不同。
  
• **自我编辑方法的优势与局限**：
  - [xianshou] 认为自我编辑方法通过优化模型如何重组信息来提高学习效果，展示了模型能够发现更好的训练格式（如知识整合结果所示）。但仍存在“灾难性遗忘”问题，且计算开销大，限制了其在大多数场景中的应用。不过在需要最佳信息保留的高价值文档处理中，可能有价值。

• **持续学习的现状与挑战**：
  - [libraryofbabel] 关注LLM在部署后持续学习（如通过持续微调）的能力，并提出当前的瓶颈（如成本、模型崩溃）可能阻碍其实用性。认为当前更多关注于训练过程的改进，而忽略了部署后的学习能力。

• **LLM学习与人类智能的差异**：
  - [perrygeo] 强调LLM的学习与推理过程是分离的，与人类智能的持续反馈过程不同。LLM训练和部署后不会进一步学习，这让人们对AGI的近未来产生误解。

• **数据限制与合成数据的重要性**：
  - [khalic] 引用研究预测到2028年所有公开的文本数据将被用尽，未来的进展将依赖于合成数据增强。提出通过元训练一个专门生成合成数据的模型，以提高数据效率。

• **技术实现与创新性讨论**：
  - [yahoozoo] 质疑该方法的创新性，认为只是对LoRA适配器进行微调并合并到原模型中，使用了HuggingFace库中的现有技术。

• **优化与调试的困难**：
  - [b0a04gl] 提出在使用奖励信号优化表示格式时，如何确保其与任务的一致性，以及模型在自我编辑过程中如何调试的问题，尤其是当错误输出发生时如何判断来源。

补充讨论：
• **命名与幽默评论**：
  - [mackenziebowes] 和 [bravesoul2] 以幽默的方式讨论了技术的命名和未来发展。
  
• **技术入门需求**：
  - [bigicaptain] 表达了对如何开始使用该技术的需求。

争议焦点：

Title:
Self-Adapting Language Models
Authors:
Adam Zweiger
,
Jyothish Pari
,
Han Guo
,
Ekin Akyürek
,
Yoon Kim
,
Pulkit Agrawal
View a PDF of the paper titled Self-Adapting Language Models, by Adam Zweiger and 5 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) are powerful but static; they lack mechanisms to adapt their weights in response to new tasks, knowledge, or examples. We introduce Self-Adapting LLMs (SEAL), a framework that enables LLMs to self-adapt by generating their own finetuning data and update directives. Given a new input, the model produces a self-edit-a generation that may restructure the information in different ways, specify optimization hyperparameters, or invoke tools for data augmentation and gradient-based updates. Through supervised finetuning (SFT), these self-edits result in persistent weight updates, enabling lasting adaptation. To train the model to produce effective self-edits, we use a reinforcement learning loop with the downstream performance of the updated model as the reward signal. Unlike prior approaches that rely on separate adaptation modules or auxiliary networks, SEAL directly uses the model's own generation to control its adaptation process. Experiments on knowledge incorporation and few-shot generalization show that SEAL is a promising step toward language models capable of self-directed adaptation. Our website and code is available at

44271284.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为SEAL（Self-Adapting Language Models）的框架，使大型语言模型（LLMs）能够通过生成自己的微调数据和更新指令来进行自我适应。SEAL利用模型自生成内容来调整其权重，实现持续适应，而不依赖额外的适应模块。通过监督微调（SFT）和强化学习，SEAL在知识整合和少样本泛化任务中展现了良好的效果，是语言模型自我适应的重要一步。相关代码和网站已提供。
44271284.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于自适应大型语言模型（LLM）的讨论，包括其学习机制、持续学习（on-the-job learning）的现状与挑战、以及模型自我编辑和调试的困难。

不同观点：
• **NEAT与模型权重进化的比较**：
  - [gavinray] 提到NEAT算法通过演化网络拓扑来解决问题，而该论文中的方法则是演化权重。两者都是解决相似问题但方式不同。
  
• **自我编辑方法的优势与局限**：
  - [xianshou] 认为自我编辑方法通过优化模型如何重组信息来提高学习效果，展示了模型能够发现更好的训练格式（如知识整合结果所示）。但仍存在“灾难性遗忘”问题，且计算开销大，限制了其在大多数场景中的应用。不过在需要最佳信息保留的高价值文档处理中，可能有价值。

• **持续学习的现状与挑战**：
  - [libraryofbabel] 关注LLM在部署后持续学习（如通过持续微调）的能力，并提出当前的瓶颈（如成本、模型崩溃）可能阻碍其实用性。认为当前更多关注于训练过程的改进，而忽略了部署后的学习能力。

• **LLM学习与人类智能的差异**：
  - [perrygeo] 强调LLM的学习与推理过程是分离的，与人类智能的持续反馈过程不同。LLM训练和部署后不会进一步学习，这让人们对AGI的近未来产生误解。

• **数据限制与合成数据的重要性**：
  - [khalic] 引用研究预测到2028年所有公开的文本数据将被用尽，未来的进展将依赖于合成数据增强。提出通过元训练一个专门生成合成数据的模型，以提高数据效率。

• **技术实现与创新性讨论**：
  - [yahoozoo] 质疑该方法的创新性，认为只是对LoRA适配器进行微调并合并到原模型中，使用了HuggingFace库中的现有技术。

• **优化与调试的困难**：
  - [b0a04gl] 提出在使用奖励信号优化表示格式时，如何确保其与任务的一致性，以及模型在自我编辑过程中如何调试的问题，尤其是当错误输出发生时如何判断来源。

补充讨论：
• **命名与幽默评论**：
  - [mackenziebowes] 和 [bravesoul2] 以幽默的方式讨论了技术的命名和未来发展。
  
• **技术入门需求**：
  - [bigicaptain] 表达了对如何开始使用该技术的需求。

争议焦点：
• **自我编辑方法的实际应用价值和创新性**：部分评论质疑该方法的创新性和实用性，尤其是计算开销大、调试困难等问题是否会限制其实际应用。

data.title: If the moon were only 1 pixel: A tediously accurate solar system model (2014)
data.author: sdoering
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要描述了太阳系中各行星之间的巨大距离，强调太空中的大部分区域都是空的。从地球到火星的旅程需要约七个月，而像木星这样的行星则更远。行星间的距离因其绕太阳的轨道位置而变化，因此准确的星际旅行需要考虑这些变化。由于太空极为空旷，大多数地图并不按实际比例绘制。文章还提到人类大脑难以理解和处理如此巨大的时间和空间尺度，常借助比喻和模型来尝试理解，但这些往往不够直观和令人满意。最终，文章强调了太空中“虚无”的本质以及人类理解这些概念的局限性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕网页上以1像素代表月球的太阳系比例可视化，用户们讨论了该可视化的效果、技术细节、教育意义以及相关的联想和体验。

不同观点：
• amelius认为光速的缓慢和星际距离的遥远让人感到一切遥不可及，甚至认为我们在到达另一颗恒星之前可能会拥有全息甲板技术。
• amiga386赞赏了该网页使用简单的HTML/CSS技术，特别是通过绝对定位和大left值来实现行星位置的排列。
• tomxor分享了一个仅用192字节准确展示太阳系的代码链接，强调了其在像素和时间比例上的准确性。
• andersco指出这是一个多年后仍令人惊叹的体验，并提供了相关讨论的链接。
• technothrasher回忆起小学时使用过的时间轴卷轴，帮助理解地质年代的跨度，与该网页的可视化有异曲同工之妙。

补充讨论：
• dang提供了多个与“如果月球只有1像素”主题相关的历史讨论链接，显示该话题在不同时间点的讨论热度。
• susam分享了自己使用POV-Ray绘制太阳系行星的经历，并讨论了在平面与轨道视角之间的选择及其局限性，认为交互式页面更能传达太阳系的规模。
• robin_reala强调了光速切换功能让人深刻感受到宇宙的空旷，尤其是在等待8分钟才能看到地球出现的时候。
• jethkl提到世界上有许多实际比例的太阳系模型，有些甚至可以通过步行或骑行体验。
• computator通过计算和比喻解释了行星在极大距离下仍然可见的原因，比如用硬币距离的比喻来说明。
• CapsAdmin表示尽管看过许多关于宇宙规模的类比，但这次体验特别震撼，尤其是光速的缓慢感。
• j_m_b推荐了Stephen Hawking's Genius中的可视化，认为其是理解太阳系规模的优秀实例。
• kennu抱怨使用鼠标滚轮进行数十万公里的滚动非常费力，最终放弃。
• Symmetry指出水星和冥王星的相对大小，通过照片对比说明了这些行星和一些已知卫星的大小关系。
• gary17the以幽默的方式反思了宇宙的广阔与个人生活中如房贷等现实问题之间的对比。

争议焦点：
• 用户对网页技术实现方式和效果有不同看法，但整体上都认可其教育意义和震撼感。

That was about 10 million km (6,213,710 mi) just now.
Pretty empty out here.
Here comes our first planet...
As it turns out, things are pretty far apart.
We’ll be coming up on a new planet soon. Sit tight.
Most of space is just space.
Halfway home.
Destination: Mars!
It would take about seven months to travel this distance in a spaceship.
Better be some good in-flight entertainment.
In case you're wondering, you'd need about 2000 feature-length movies to occupy that many waking hours.
Sit back and relax. Jupiter is more than 3 times as far as we just traveled.
When are we gonna be there?
Seriously. When are we gonna be there?
This is where we might at least see some asteroids to wake us up.
Too bad they're all too small to appear on this map.
I spy, with my little eye... something black.
If you were on a road trip, driving at 75mi/hr, it would have taken you over 500 years to get here from earth.
All these distances are just averages, mind you.
The distance between planets really depends on where the two planets are in their orbits around the sun.
So if you're planning on taking a trip to Jupiter, you might want to use a different map.
If you plan it right, you can actually move relatively quickly between planets.
The New Horizons space craft that launched in 2006 only took 13 months to get to Jupiter.
Don't worry. It'll take a lot less than 13 months to scroll there.
Pretty close to Jupiter now.
Sorry. That was a lie before. Now we really are pretty close.
Lots of time to think out here...
Pop the champagne! We just passed 1 billion km.
I guess this is why most maps of the solar system aren't drawn to scale.
It's not hard to draw the planets.
It's the empty space that's a problem.
Most space charts leave out the most significant part – all the space.
We're used to dealing with things at a much smaller scale than this.
When it comes to things like the age of the earth, the number of snowflakes in Siberia, the national debt...
Those things are too much for our brains to handle.
We need to reduce things down to something we can see or experience directly in order to understand them.
We're always trying to come up with metaphors for big numbers. Even so, they never seem to work.
Let's try a few metaphors anyway...
You would need
of these screens lined up side-by-side to show this whole map at once.
If this map was printed from a quality printer (300 pixels per inch) the earth would be invisible, and the width of the paper would need to be 475 feet.
475 feet is about 1 and 1/2 football fields.
Even though we don’t really understand them, a lot can happen within these massive lengths of time and space.
A drop of water can carve out a canyon.
An amoeba can become a dolphin.
A star can collapse on itself.
It’s easy to disregard nothingness because there’s no thought available to encapsulate it. There’s no metaphor that fits because, by definition, once the nothingness becomes tangible, it ceases to exist.
It’s a good thing we have these tiny stars and planets, otherwise we’d have no point of reference at all.
We’d be surrounded by this stuff that our minds weren’t built to understand.
All this emptiness really could drive you nuts. For instance, if you’re in a sensory deprivation tank for too long, your brain starts to make things up. You see and hear things that aren’t there.
The brain isn't built to handle "empty."
"Sorry, Humanity," says Evolution. "What with all the jaguars trying to eat you, the parasites in your fur, and the never-ending need for a decent steak, I was a little busy. I didn’t exactly have time to come up with a way to conceive of vast stretches of nothingness."
Neurologically speaking, we really only deal with matter of a certain size, and energy of a few select wavelengths. For everything else, we have to make up mental models and see if they match up to the tiny shreds of hard evidence that actually feel real.
The mental models provided by mathematics are extremely helpful when trying to make sense of these vast distances, but still...
Abstraction is pretty unsatisfying.
When you hear people talk about how, "there’s more to this universe than our minds can conceive of" it's usually a way to get you to go along with a half-baked plot point about UFOs or super-powers in a sci-fi series that you're watching late at night when you can’t get to sleep.
Even when Shakespeare wrote: "There are more things in heaven and earth, Horatio, Than are dreamt of in your philosophy” – he's basically trying to give us a loophole to make the ghost in the story more believable.
But all this empty space, these things of a massive scale, really are more than our minds can conceive of. The maps and metaphors fail to do them justice.
You look at one tiny dot, then you look for the next tiny dot. Everything in between is inconsequential and fairly boring.
Emptiness is actually ever

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何在开发中利用LLM（大型语言模型）和相关工具进行高效开发和协作

不同观点：
• [kasey_junk] 认为可以直接使用Claude（一种LLM工具）来实现所需功能，只需将现有的指令输入模型，模型很可能会直接生成符合要求的结果，不需要太多迭代。
• [squircle] 提出利用README或文档文件夹作为唯一真相来源，结合构建步骤和系统提示，保持人类在开发循环中，实现真正的快速迭代开发。这种方法强调了人类参与和可逆计算的重要性。
• [DonHopkins] 介绍了Leela AI开发的LLOOOOMM系统，这是一种基于角色的AI系统，利用LLM模拟角色和进化协议。该系统通过YAML和Markdown文件存储角色的本质和实现，每个角色都是特定领域的专家，可以被调用以提供专业意见。该观点强调了角色协作、持久化上下文和协议进化的独特优势。

补充讨论：
• [squircle] 提到自己已经在使用类似的工具和方法，并通过Rust和JS开发了部分工具，证明了其有效性。他还提出了对工具未来发展的困惑，例如是否应该开源或商业化。
• [DonHopkins] 详细描述了LLOOOOMM系统中各种角色的功能和应用，包括Brewster Kahle的归档协议、Ted Nelson的同理查询、Alan Kay的“游戏→学习→提升”协议等。这些角色和协议展示了系统的广泛应用和潜在价值。
• [LLOOOOMM角色] 展示了系统的实际应用案例，例如Linus Torvalds提供Git帮助、Owl Simulation作为自我意识代码的证明、以及多角色协作设计UI等。这些案例突出了系统的实用性和灵活性。
• [LLOOOOMM系统的自我描述和演示] 强调了系统的自我描述和多层次自引用特性，通过视频演示和角色互动，展示了系统的复杂性和独特性。

争议焦点：
• 对于LLM工具的应用方式存在不同看法。[kasey_junk] 倾向于直接使用LLM生成代码，而 [squircle] 则强调了人类在开发循环中的重要性和工具的可控性。[DonHopkins] 则展示了一种全新的角色协作和协议进化方式，突出了系统的复杂性和创新性。

总结：讨论主要围绕LLM工具的应用和开发方法展开，涉及到直接生成代码、文档驱动开发、角色协作系统等多种方式，展示了不同的开发理念和实践方法。

• [squircle] 提到自己已经在使用类似的工具和方法，并通过Rust和JS开发了部分工具，证明了其有效性。他还提出了对工具未来发展的困惑，例如是否应该开源或商业化。
• [DonHopkins] 详细描述了LLOOOOMM系统中各种角色的功能和应用，包括Brewster Kahle的归档协议、Ted Nelson的同理查询、Alan Kay的“游戏→学习→提升”协议等。这些角色和协议展示了系统的广泛应用和潜在价值。
• [LLOOOOMM角色] 展示了系统的实际应用案例，例如Linus Torvalds提供Git帮助、Owl Simulation作为自我意识代码的证明、以及多角色协作设计UI等。这些案例突出了系统的实用性和灵活性。
• [LLOOOOMM系统的自我描述和演示] 强调了系统的自我描述和多层次自引用特性，通过视频演示和角色互动，展示了系统的复杂性和独特性。

争议焦点：
• 对于LLM工具的应用方式存在不同看法。[kasey_junk] 倾向于直接使用LLM生成代码，而 [squircle] 则强调了人类在开发循环中的重要性和工具的可控性。[DonHopkins] 则展示了一种全新的角色协作和协议进化方式，突出了系统的复杂性和创新性。

总结：讨论主要围绕LLM工具的应用和开发方法展开，涉及到直接生成代码、文档驱动开发、角色协作系统等多种方式，展示了不同的开发理念和实践方法。

data.title: First 2D, non-silicon computer developed
data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary: 宾夕法尼亚州立大学的研究团队开发了世界上首个基于二维材料的非硅计算机。该计算机使用了两种二维材料——二硫化钼（n型）和二硒化钨（p型）——来构建互补金属氧化物半导体（CMOS）计算机，突破了传统硅材料的限制。与硅不同，这些二维材料在原子厚度下仍能保持其优异的电子特性，有助于实现更薄、更快、更节能的电子设备。尽管该计算机的运行频率较低，仅能执行简单的逻辑操作，但这是二维材料计算机领域的重大进展，为未来电子技术的发展奠定了基础。研究人员表示，尽管还需要进一步优化，但这一成果标志着二维材料在电子学应用中的重要里程碑。

44261118.article_content:
Research
World’s first 2D, non-silicon computer developed
This conceptual illustration of a computer based on 2D molecules displays an actual scanning electron microscope image of the computer fabricated by a team by researchers at Penn State. The keyboard features highlighted keys labeled with the abbreviations for molybdenum disulfide and tungsten diselenide, representing the two 2D materials used to develop the transistors in the computer.
Credit:
Krishnendu Mukhopadhyay/Penn State
.
All Rights Reserved
.
Expand
June 11, 2025
By
Ashley WennersHerron
UNIVERSITY PARK, Pa. — Silicon is king in the semiconductor technology that underpins smartphones, computers, electric vehicles and more, but its crown may be slipping, according to a team led by researchers at Penn State. In a world first, they used two-dimensional (2D) materials, which are only an atom thick and retain their properties at that scale, unlike silicon, to develop a computer capable of simple operations.
The development, published today (June 11) in
Nature
, represents a major leap toward the realization of thinner, faster and more energy-efficient electronics, the researchers said. They created a complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS) computer — technology at the heart of nearly every modern electronic device — without relying on silicon. Instead, they used two different 2D materials to develop both types of transistors needed to control the electric current flow in CMOS computers: molybdenum disulfide for n-type transistors and tungsten diselenide for p-type transistors.
“Silicon has driven remarkable advances in electronics for decades by enabling continuous miniaturization of field-effect transistors (FETs),” said
Saptarshi Das
, the Ackley Professor of Engineering and professor of engineering science and mechanics at Penn State, who led the research. FETs control current flow using an electric field, which is produced when a voltage is applied. “However, as silicon devices shrink, their performance begins to degrade. Two-dimensional materials, by contrast, maintain their exceptional electronic properties at atomic thickness, offering a promising path forward.”
Das explained that CMOS technology requires both n-type and p-type semiconductors working together to achieve high performance at low power consumption — a key challenge that has stymied efforts to move beyond silicon. Although previous studies demonstrated small circuits based on 2D materials, scaling to complex, functional computers had remained elusive, Das said.
“That’s the key advancement of our work,” Das said. “We have demonstrated, for the first time, a CMOS computer built entirely from 2D materials, combining large area grown molybdenum disulfide and tungsten diselenide transistors.”
The team used metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) — a fabrication process that involves vaporizing ingredients, forcing a chemical reaction and depositing the products onto a substrate — to grow large sheets of molybdenum disulfide and tungsten diselenide and fabricate over 1,000 of each type of transistor. By carefully tuning the device fabrication and post-processing steps, they were able to adjust the threshold voltages of both n- and p-type transistors, enabling the construction of fully functional CMOS logic circuits.
“Our 2D CMOS computer operates at low-supply voltages with minimal power consumption and can perform simple logic operations at frequencies up to 25 kilohertz,” said first author Subir Ghosh, a doctoral student pursuing a degree in engineering science and mechanics under Das’s mentorship.
Ghosh noted that the operating frequency is low compared to conventional silicon CMOS circuits, but their computer — known as a one instruction set computer — can still perform simple logic operations.
“We also developed a computational model, calibrated using experimental data and incorporating variations between devices, to project the performance of our 2D CMOS computer and benchmark it against state-of-the-art silicon technology,” Ghosh said. “Although there remains scope for further optimization, this work marks a significant milestone in harnessing 2D materials to advance the field of electronics.”
Das agreed, explaining that more work is needed to further develop the 2D CMOS computer approach for broad use, but also emphasizing that the field is moving quickly when compared to the development of silicon technology.
“Silicon technology has been under development for about 80 years, but research into 2D materials is relatively recent, only really arising around 2010,” Das said. “We expect that the development of 2D material computers is going to be a gradual process, too, but this is a leap forward compared to the trajectory of silicon.”
Ghosh and Das credited the
2D Crystal Consortium Materials Innovation Platform
(2DCC-MIP) at Penn State with providing the facilities and tools needed to demonstrate their approach. Das is also affiliated with the
Materials Research I

data.author: AI314159
data.article_summary: Seastar是一个受Cargo启发的构建系统，旨在简化C、C++项目的构建，未来可能支持Rust和Zig。其目标是让编程、原型设计和迭代变得更加容易，尤其对于初学者。Seastar提供增量构建、自定义编译器参数、并行构建等功能，并支持C++和Rust的无缝编译。当前处于早期开发阶段，但计划实现模板生成和统一的包管理器等功能。使用Seastar需要Rust和Cargo，通过简单命令即可构建和运行示例项目。项目采用GPL-3.0许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新C++构建系统的必要性、功能、依赖管理以及命名问题

不同观点：
• scuol和dmead认为当前存在一个名为Seastar的著名C++框架，建议更改项目名称以避免混淆。此外，dmead还指出"Seastar"和"C*"等名称已存在，建议考虑新名称。
• no_circuit不推荐以Cargo为蓝本构建新系统，指出Cargo在处理全局特性及依赖元数据传播方面的不足。他们建议超越C/C++和Rust，参考Bazel和Buck 2的功能，尤其是它们在多语言和分布式构建方面的优势。

• throwaway70985对Cargo的复杂性表示不满，表示会继续使用CMake。

Seastar
Seastar is a fast, extensible build system for C, C++, and maybe soon, Rust and Zig as well.
I believe that it should be easy to make, prototype, and iterate upon designs.
While C is still one of our most widely used languages, it makes it hard to create
programs easily, especially for beginners. Instead, Seastar aims to be more like
Rust's tooling with
cargo
, but supporting seamless compilation across more languages.
Running
Seastar is very simple to build and run. Assuming you have Cargo and Rust installed,
clone the repository,
cd
into the
example
folder, and run
cargo run -- build
to run Seastar and build the example project, or
cargo run -- run
to run the example
project. Check
example/Seastar.toml
to make sure that you have the compiler
installed and correctly set in that file.
Roadmap
Seastar is still in a very early state, and thus I wouldn't recommend using it
currently for anything serious. Below, however, you can see my roadmap, and if
you want to get updates, you can watch this repository.
Sort of working: Being able to compile and link a simple project with multiple files and include headers.
Incremental builds: The entire program shouldn't be recompiled every time a single file is changed.
Custom compiler flags: The programmer should be able to customize the compiler flags through
Seastar.toml
without needing to change the build/run commands.
Parallel builds: Compiling in parallel is faster and more efficient.
C++ support: Seastar should be able to compile and link C++ without changing options or difficult configuration.
Rust support: Seastar should be able to compile and link Rust without changing options or difficult configuration.
Easy template generation: We should be able to create templates with a single command, e.g.
seastar init --lang c
Unified package manager: a difficult goal, but it should be easy to install packages for C, C++, and Rust neatly and natively to Seastar.
If you find this project cool and want to see more , please consider leaving a star!
It supports the development of this project and is really helpful.

data.title: It’s nearly impossible to buy an original Bob Ross painting (2021)
data.author: rmason
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了为何几乎无法购买到著名电视画家鲍勃·罗斯（Bob Ross）的原作。尽管罗斯一生创作了约3万幅画作，但这些作品很少在市场上出现。罗斯通过《绘画的乐趣》节目成名，该节目在1983年至1994年间播出了381集，每集他都会完成一幅风景画。然而，这些画作大多归鲍勃·罗斯公司所有，因为根据协议，这些作品属于“雇佣创作”。罗斯去世后，这些画作由公司共同创始人安内特·科瓦尔斯基及其家人控制，约1165幅原作目前存放在公司的办公室中，并未在市场上流通。尽管市场需求旺盛，但由于公司对画作的控制，原作极少出售。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bob Ross原创画作未被出售的原因以及其艺术价值和市场需求。

不同观点：
• paxys认为，Bob Ross在世时他的画作并不抢手，是因为当时没有需求，直到2010年代互联网普及后他才爆红。现在因为数量多，如果全部出售可能会使画作贬值，所以Bob Ross公司选择控制供应以提高价格。
• solomonb指出，当代艺术市场中，新晋艺术家的画作价格往往在1万到2万美元之间，相比之下Bob Ross画作的实际市场价格偏低。
• ahofmann强调，文章最后才提到Bob Ross不希望自己的画作成为商品，这是关键信息。
• bluefirebrand认为，Bob Ross在电视上展现的形象是一个教导人们绘画乐趣的艺术家，他可能更希望人们自己绘画，而不是购买他的作品。

Why it’s nearly impossible to buy an original Bob Ross painting
Why it’s nearly impossible to buy an original Bob Ross painting
The famed TV artist was one of history’s most prolific painters. But finding Bob Ross paintings for sale is a long shot.
Zachary Crockett
Zachary Crockett
Published:
May 02, 2021
Updated:
June 13, 2025
Bob Ross is not a hard man to find.
Though he died in 1995, the late TV painter remains an omnipresent cultural staple. His Chia Pet perm, nap-inducing voice, and meme-worthy sayings — “
Happy little trees!
” — have transcended time. On
YouTube
, old episodes of his show,
The Joy of Painting
, boast ~
450m views
.
Online, you can acquire Bob Ross paints, Bob Ross brushes, Bob Ross underwear, Bob Ross coffee mugs, Bob Ross energy drinks, Bob Ross watches, and Bob Ross toasters.
But there’s one thing you won’t often see for sale: his artwork.
During his lifetime, Ross produced
tens of thousands of paintings
. Yet, only a handful of his works have popped up for sale in recent years. When they do appear, they often fetch
$10k+
and attract dozens of bids.
Why is the work of one of history’s most prolific and accessible artists so scarce on the open market?
To find out, I spoke with art gallery owners, auctioneers, art collectors, ex-colleagues who worked with Ross, and the president of Bob Ross, Inc. — the company that preserves his legacy.
The man behind the canvas
Born in Daytona, Florida, in 1942, Ross dropped out of school in 9th grade to work with his father, a carpenter.
At 18, he joined the Air Force and moved to Alaska, where he’d spend the next 20 years as a drill sergeant, screaming at recruits. He was such a hard-ass that he earned the
nickname
“Bust ’em up Bobby.”
But his life changed when he discovered art.
Inspired by the TV painter
Bill Alexander
, he started painting landscapes on gold mining pans and selling them at local markets in Alaska.
His income from painting soon surpassed what he made in the military. So, in 1981, he migrated back to Florida, trained under Alexander, and became a certified painting instructor.
Bob Ross strikes a happy pose (Photo: Acey Harper/The LIFE Images Collection via Getty Images)
Now, here’s where things took a wild turn for Ross:
One of his students,
Annette Kowalski
, was “mesmerized” by the jolly painter and encouraged him to strike out on his own.
They pooled together their life savings, launched
Bob Ross, Inc.
, and set out to make Ross into a TV star.
A PBS executive gave them a shot.
The show —
The Joy of Painting
, which aired between 1983 and 1994
— was a huge hit and was broadcast on
~300 stations
to
80m+
people every day.
In each 27-minute episode, Ross would paint one landscape from start to finish, shepherding viewers through his process with a soothing disposition, entertaining commentary, and an occasional guest appearance by his
pet squirrel
, Peapod.
Ross didn’t get paid for his shows. But Bob Ross, Inc. — which he partially owned — used the platform to sell paints, art supplies, workshops, instructional videos, and merchandise. By 1991, it was a
$15m/year ($29m today)
enterprise.
The actual paintings, though, were largely an afterthought.
Over the course of his career, Ross filmed
381 episodes
of
The Joy of Painting
. For each episode, he painted
3 versions
of the same artwork — one before, one during, and one after taping.
But his TV career only scratched the surface of his total output.
Pre-fame, in Alaska, he sold thousands of paintings. And even while famous, he painted nearly every day at seminars, events, and charity auctions in between tapings.
All told, Bob Ross
churned out
~
30k paintings
in his lifetime — nearly 3x the output of Picasso, a prolific painter in his own right.
Zachary Crockett / The Hustle (painting © Bob Ross Inc.)
For years, collectors and fans have clamored to own their own piece of Bob Ross lore. Multiple art dealers told
The Hustle
that demand for his work is extraordinarily robust.
But Ross paintings are a bit like diamonds: vast in volume, scarce on the open market.
Major auction houses — Christie’s, Sotheby’s, Phillips — have no Bob Ross sales history. Craigslist draws a goose egg. A scan of eBay only turns up
3 sales
in the last 6 months, 2 of which are of dubious origin.
Where the heck are those 30k paintings?
Bob Ross, Incorporated
As a part of Ross’s agreement with Bob Ross, Inc., the paintings he created for TV were
work for hire
, meaning the company maintained ownership of his work.
When Ross died in 1995, Bob Ross, Inc. (and thus, the paintings) became the sole property of Annette Kowalski and her husband, Walt.
Today,
1,165
Bob Ross originals — a trove worth millions of dollars —
sit in cardboard boxes
inside the company’s nondescript office building in Herndon, Virginia.
Joan Kowalski
, Annette’s daughter, and the current president of Bob Ross, Inc., tells
The Hustle
that the company had never really given the paintings much thought.
“The paintings have always just s
44284723.article_summary: 本文探讨了为何几乎无法购买到著名电视画家鲍勃·罗斯（Bob Ross）的原作。尽管罗斯一生创作了约3万幅画作，但这些作品很少在市场上出现。罗斯通过《绘画的乐趣》节目成名，该节目在1983年至1994年间播出了381集，每集他都会完成一幅风景画。然而，这些画作大多归鲍勃·罗斯公司所有，因为根据协议，这些作品属于“雇佣创作”。罗斯去世后，这些画作由公司共同创始人安内特·科瓦尔斯基及其家人控制，约1165幅原作目前存放在公司的办公室中，并未在市场上流通。尽管市场需求旺盛，但由于公司对画作的控制，原作极少出售。

data.article_summary: 《The Hobo Code: An Introduction to the Hieroglyphic Language of Early 1900s Train-Hoppers》一文介绍了20世纪初美国流浪打工者的独特文化。这些人被称为“hobo”，他们通过非法搭乘货运火车在全国各地流动，为了生存，他们创造了一种秘密符号语言——"hobo代码"。这些符号被画在墙壁或水塔上，用以指引方向、警示危险或标记资源。然而，尽管有许多关于这些符号的传说，实际证据表明它们的广泛使用可能被夸大。hobo们通过这些符号和故事塑造并隐藏自己的形象，这种流浪精神在现代如城市涂鸦中仍能看到其影响。文章还提到hobo的伦理守则，强调自力更生、诚实和同情。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕涂鸦和流浪者符号的文化和历史意义的讨论

不同观点：
• JKCalhoun分享了自己几十年前在阿拉斯加搭便车的个人经历。他提到在偏僻的地方看到电话杆上刻有许多来自不同国家的人的名字和日期，这让他感到一丝宽慰，因为知道自己不是唯一在那里等待便车的人。这个观点侧重于个人经历和对流浪者符号的情感反应。

• burningChrome则从学术角度讨论了涂鸦文化，尤其是与火车相关的涂鸦。他提到火车上的涂鸦包含了许多流浪者的交流符号和哲学思考，并且指出这种文化至今仍然活跃，尤其是在社交媒体上有很多人记录和分享这些涂鸦。这个观点强调涂鸦作为一种文化现象和交流方式的存在和延续。

• p1anecrazy提供了对流浪者符号的学术研究视角，引用了Richard Sproat的书，并将流浪者符号与德国流浪者使用的符号进行了比较。他指出这些符号的研究往往与犯罪相关，因为很多分析来自警方的调查。这个观点关注的是对流浪者符号的学术研究和其历史背景。

补充讨论：
• JKCalhoun的经历提供了一种对流浪者符号的个人情感视角，强调这些符号在孤立环境中的心理安慰作用。
• burningChrome的观点揭示了涂鸦文化的广泛性和持续性，尤其是在火车上的表现，并指出了现代社交媒体在记录和传播这种文化中的作用。
• p1anecrazy引入了对流浪者符号的学术研究，特别是其与犯罪调查的关联，提供了一种更为历史和学术的视角。

争议焦点：
• 对流浪者符号的解读和其主要功能的理解存在差异。JKCalhoun从个人经历出发，强调其情感作用；burningChrome侧重其文化交流功能；而p1anecrazy则从学术和历史的角度分析其与犯罪的关联。

总结：讨论围绕流浪者符号和涂鸦的文化意义展开，涉及个人经历、文化现象和学术研究等多重角度，展示了这一现象的复杂性和多面性。

The Hobo Code: An Introduction to the Hieroglyphic Language of Early 1900s Train-Hoppers
in
History
|   	August 22nd, 2018
2 Comments
Many of us now use the word
hobo
to refer to any home­less indi­vid­ual, but back in the Amer­i­ca of the late 19th and ear­ly 20th cen­tu­ry, to be a hobo meant some­thing more. It meant, specif­i­cal­ly, to count your­self as part of a robust cul­ture of itin­er­ant labor­ers who criss-crossed the coun­try by hitch­ing ille­gal rides on freight trains. Liv­ing such a lifestyle on the mar­gins of soci­ety demand­ed the mas­tery of cer­tain tech­niques as well as a body of secret knowl­edge, an aspect of the hey­day of hobodom sym­bol­ized in the “hobo code,” a spe­cial hiero­glyph­ic lan­guage explained in
the Vox video above
.
“Wan­der­ing from place to place and per­form­ing odd jobs in exchange for food and mon­ey, hobos were met with both open arms and firearms,”
writes Antique Archae­ol­o­gy’s Sarah Buck­holtz
. “From ille­gal­ly jump­ing trains to steal­ing scraps from a farm­ers mar­ket, the hobo com­mu­ni­ty need­ed to cre­ate a secret lan­guage to warn and wel­come fel­low hobos that were either new to town or just pass­ing through.”
The code, writ­ten on brick walls, bases of water tow­ers, or any oth­er sur­face that did­n’t move, “assigned cir­cles and arrows for gen­er­al direc­tions like, where to find a meal or the best place to camp. Hash­tags sig­naled dan­ger ahead, like bad water or an inhos­pitable town.”
Hash­tags
sounds a bit Mil­len­ni­al for hobo cul­ture, but on some lev­el the term does make sense. Some of the abstract­ed sym­bols of the hobo code look a bit more like emo­ji: a loco­mo­tive mean­ing “good place to catch a train,” a build­ing with a barred door mean­ing “this is a well-guard­ed house,” a cat mean­ing “a kind lady lives here.” But how much use did the hobo code actu­al­ly see? “The prob­lem is, all this infor­ma­tion came from hobos, a group that took pride in their elu­sive­ness and embell­ished sto­ry­telling,” says the Vox video’s nar­ra­tor. “The truth is, there real­ly isn’t any evi­dence that these signs were as wide­ly used as the lit­er­a­ture sug­gests.”
“Hobos used their mythol­o­gy as a kind of cov­er,” says hobo his­to­ri­an
Bill Daniel
. “The tall tales, the draw­ings, even the books” — espe­cial­ly vol­umes penned by
“A‑No.1,”
the most famous hobo of them all — “were ways to project an image of them­selves that both blew them up, but also kept them hid­den.” Yet hobo ways, which encom­passed even an
eth­i­cal code
that we’ve
pre­vi­ous­ly fea­tured here on Open Cul­ture
, have their descen­dants. Take, for instance, the hobo prac­tice of writ­ing their nick­names, or “monikers,” on trains and else­where to show the world where they’d been and where they were head­ed. The line to mod­ern urban graf­fi­ti almost draws itself, espe­cial­ly in the prac­tice of
sub­way-car “bomb­ing”
in 1970s and 80s New York. The hobo has gone, but the char­ac­ter­is­ti­cal­ly hardy hobo spir­it finds a way to live on.
Relat­ed Con­tent:
The Hobo Eth­i­cal Code of 1889: 15 Rules for Liv­ing a Self-Reliant, Hon­est & Com­pas­sion­ate Life
How to Write in Cuneiform, the Old­est Writ­ing Sys­tem in the World: A Short, Charm­ing Intro­duc­tion
You Could Soon Be Able to Text with 2,000 Ancient Egypt­ian Hiero­glyphs
Google Puts Online 10,000 Works of Street Art from Across the Globe
‘Boom Boom’ and ‘Hobo Blues’: Great Per­for­mances by John Lee Hook­er
Based in Seoul,
Col­in Mar­shall
writes and broad­casts on cities and cul­ture. His projects include the book
The State­less City: a Walk through 21st-Cen­tu­ry Los Ange­les
and the video series
The City in Cin­e­ma
. Fol­low him on Twit­ter at

data.title: How fast can the RPython GC allocate?
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者对RPython垃圾收集器（GC）对象分配速度的基准测试过程。作者编写了一个简单的RPython程序，通过循环创建对象来测量分配速度。为了避免静态优化移除分配代码，作者使用了一种技巧，保持两个对象同时存活。基准测试包括初始化和不初始化对象字段两种情况。

在64位架构下，每次分配大约需要16字节。测试结果显示，未初始化字段时，分配速度为34.348 GB/s，初始化字段时为29.692 GB/s。相比之下，使用Boehm GC的版本速度较慢，未初始化和初始化时的速度分别为1.532 GB/s和1.538 GB/s，这是因为Boehm GC使用保守的栈扫描，无法移动对象。

作者还使用`perf`工具获取了更详细的性能统计数据，结果显示RPython GC在循环中达到了每周期超过5条指令的效率。这表明RPython GC在对象分配上的性能表现相当出色。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同内存分配器（allocator）的性能比较，包括在特定硬件上的分配速度、指令数量以及与传统分配器（如malloc/free）的对比。

不同观点：
• **Kragen的观点**：Kragen指出，在CF Bolz的AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 7840U机器上，每个纳秒有1-2次分配，每次分配大约11条指令。这比Kragen自己的C语言分配器kmregion快2-4倍。Kragen的分配器在快速路径上也有类似数量的指令，但他测试的硬件较慢，并且测试的是16字节初始化对象且没有垃圾回收（GC）。kmregion的速度大约是malloc/free的10倍，但他并不强烈推荐使用kmregion，因为该工具从未被用于任何重大项目，只是作为一个概念验证。

• **pizlonator的观点**：pizlonator认为，CF Bolz的分配器比Boehm快，并不是因为保守栈扫描（conservative stack scanning），而是因为使用了不同的算法。他指出，可以通过保守栈扫描来移动对象，JavaScriptCore曾使用过这种方法。最快的非移动收集器（non-moving collectors）在分配速度上可以与最快的移动收集器（moving collectors）相媲美。他提到了JavaScriptCore的bump'n'pop分配器、Fil-C的SIMD turbosweep方法以及Immix方法等不同实现方式。

• **forrestthewoods的观点**：forrestthewoods对11指令和2.1周期每次分配的度量表示怀疑，认为这不符合常理。他引用自己几年前的一个基准测试，p95为25纳秒，而p99.9则在几十微秒的范围。他认为“GC占用2%的时间”可能对结果有很大影响，并表示需要看到真实的工作负载才能相信这些数据。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于分配器的性能指标是否可信，尤其是对于极端优化场景下的纳秒级分配速度，部分参与者表示怀疑。
• 不同分配器的算法实现方式被讨论，包括保守栈扫描、对象移动、bump'n'pop和SIMD turbosweep等方法的优劣。
• 硬件对性能的影响也被提及，不同测试环境下的结果可能会有显著差异。

在64位架构下，每次分配大约需要16字节。测试结果显示，未初始化字段时，分配速度为34.348 GB/s，初始化字段时为29.692 GB/s。相比之下，使用Boehm GC的版本速度较慢，未初始化和初始化时的速度分别为1.532 GB/s和1.538 GB/s，这是因为Boehm GC使用保守的栈扫描，无法移动对象。

作者还使用`perf`工具获取了更详细的性能统计数据，结果显示RPython GC在循环中达到了每周期超过5条指令的效率。这表明RPython GC在对象分配上的性能表现相当出色。
44284592.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同内存分配器（allocator）的性能比较，包括在特定硬件上的分配速度、指令数量以及与传统分配器（如malloc/free）的对比。

不同观点：
• **Kragen的观点**：Kragen指出，在CF Bolz的AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 7840U机器上，每个纳秒有1-2次分配，每次分配大约11条指令。这比Kragen自己的C语言分配器kmregion快2-4倍。Kragen的分配器在快速路径上也有类似数量的指令，但他测试的硬件较慢，并且测试的是16字节初始化对象且没有垃圾回收（GC）。kmregion的速度大约是malloc/free的10倍，但他并不强烈推荐使用kmregion，因为该工具从未被用于任何重大项目，只是作为一个概念验证。

• **pizlonator的观点**：pizlonator认为，CF Bolz的分配器比Boehm快，并不是因为保守栈扫描（conservative stack scanning），而是因为使用了不同的算法。他指出，可以通过保守栈扫描来移动对象，JavaScriptCore曾使用过这种方法。最快的非移动收集器（non-moving collectors）在分配速度上可以与最快的移动收集器（moving collectors）相媲美。他提到了JavaScriptCore的bump'n'pop分配器、Fil-C的SIMD turbosweep方法以及Immix方法等不同实现方式。

• **forrestthewoods的观点**：forrestthewoods对11指令和2.1周期每次分配的度量表示怀疑，认为这不符合常理。他引用自己几年前的一个基准测试，p95为25纳秒，而p99.9则在几十微秒的范围。他认为“GC占用2%的时间”可能对结果有很大影响，并表示需要看到真实的工作负载才能相信这些数据。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于分配器的性能指标是否可信，尤其是对于极端优化场景下的纳秒级分配速度，部分参与者表示怀疑。
• 不同分配器的算法实现方式被讨论，包括保守栈扫描、对象移动、bump'n'pop和SIMD turbosweep等方法的优劣。
• 硬件对性能的影响也被提及，不同测试环境下的结果可能会有显著差异。

data.author: civilaircraft
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了即将上市的科技公司IPO信息平台"IPOChatter"。用户可以追踪最受关注的科技公司，设置个人提醒，获取实时通知和最新新闻。页面还提供公司状态、预期上市时间、信心指数等详细信息。用户需登录或注册账户，并同意数据处理条款。注册时，用户可选择是否接收营销信息和分析跟踪，并可在账户设置中随时撤销同意。同时，用户可以提交IPO相关新闻，参与讨论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IPO投资的合理性及特定公司是否应列入IPO名单

不同观点：
• [candiddevmike的观点] IPO投资风险高且不确定性大。他认为大多数IPO公司的财务数据被粉饰过，通常在短期内股价会下跌。因此，他认为投资者很难在IPO时做出明智的购买决策，最好等市场稳定后再做决定。
  - 论据：财务数据被“粉饰”（juiced），即可能经过美化；
  - 例子：IPO后股价通常下跌；
  - 结论：建议等待市场稳定再投资。

• [davedx的观点] 对某些未计划上市的公司被列入IPO名单表示质疑。他认为像SpaceX和Stripe这样没有上市计划的公司被列入名单是不合理的，仅仅提到名字没有实际意义。
  - 论据：这些公司没有明确的上市意图；
  - 例子：SpaceX和Stripe；
  - 结论：认为这种“点名”是不严肃且无意义的。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于IPO投资的可靠性和特定公司是否应被列入IPO名单。candiddevmike强调IPO市场的高度不确定性和潜在风险，而davedx则关注名单中未计划上市公司的相关性。
- 两者讨论的核心区别在于：一个是针对IPO市场的普遍风险，另一个是关于IPO名单中公司选择的合理性。

data.title: Cure Dolly's Japanese Grammar Lessons
data.author: agnishom
data.article_summary: Cure Dolly脚本是一个提供日语学习课程的网站。该网站以Markdown格式呈现，方便用户快速访问和阅读所有Dolly的日语课程内容。用户可以从第一课开始学习，并且网站简洁实用，便于系统地学习日语。此外，网站还包含关于页面，介绍相关信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cure Dolly的日语教学视频及其影响

不同观点：
• [joshdavham] 介绍Cure Dolly的背景，强调她是一位通过虚拟形象教授基础日语语法的YouTube博主，拥有一定数量的忠实粉丝，并且在她去世后仍然受到怀念。
• [kochikame] 表示自己有较高的日语水平，并认为Cure Dolly的内容对初学者非常有帮助，尤其是她提出的一些观察和见解能够帮助学习者节省自己摸索的时间。
• [Macha] 认为Cure Dolly的指南对日语初学者是一个很好的起点，但提醒观众不要过于认真对待她所谓的“只需这些就够了”的宣传，因为这些内容更偏向入门级别，而非完整指南。
• [greybox] 对Cure Dolly的视频给予高度评价，认为这些视频对日语初学者非常有帮助，尽管有时她会发表一些关于教科书的奇怪言论，但整体内容质量很高。同时表达了对视频制作者努力的感谢和Cure Dolly的悼念。
• [amiga386] 对Cure Dolly对日语语法符号（如"だ"）的解释表示困惑和不解，附上了一张图片以示疑问。

补充讨论：
• [happa] 提到另一个学习日语的好资源，提供了一个链接，并未直接讨论Cure Dolly的内容，而是提供了其他学习途径。
• [wyager] 提到自己曾调查过Cure Dolly的真实身份，并声称有一些可信的证据表明她与Silver Sisterhood（即所谓的“女同性恋鞭打崇拜”）有关联，这一团体因早期文字冒险游戏产业的活动而闻名。这个评论引入了关于Cure Dolly背景的争议，可能引发对其身份和动机的讨论。

争议焦点：
• Cure Dolly的身份背景，尤其是[wyager]提到的与Silver Sisterhood可能的关联，可能影响观众对她内容的可信度和动机的看法。
• Cure Dolly对日语语法符号（如"だ"）的解释，[amiga386]对此表示困惑，显示出对她某些具体教学内容的质疑。

总结：
讨论主要围绕Cure Dolly的日语教学视频的价值和影响展开，有观众对其内容表示高度赞赏，认为对初学者很有帮助，但也有人提醒不要过度依赖她的“入门级”内容，同时对其身份背景和某些具体教学点存在争议。

data.title: Why SSL was renamed to TLS in late 90s (2014)
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 这篇文章回顾了90年代中期Netscape与微软在浏览器大战期间的竞争，特别是在安全协议SSL上的较量。Netscape最初开发了SSL协议，但SSL 2.0存在缺陷。微软为了竞争推出了基于SSL 2.0的PCT协议。Netscape则开发了SSL 3.0以解决这些问题，但行业内希望避免协议分裂。经过协商，双方同意让IETF标准化该协议，导致SSL 3.0被修改并重命名为TLS 1.0（实质上是SSL 3.1），从而避免了专有标准的竞争。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SSL/TLS协议的发展、区别及其历史背景

不同观点：
• [ekr____] 指出SSL和TLS的不同版本之间存在显著差异，特别是SSLv2、SSLv3、TLS 1.0、TLS 1.1和TLS 1.2的演变过程，强调每个版本在设计时都考虑了自动协商版本的机制，以确保客户端和服务器可以独立升级而不影响连接。
• [Timothycquinn] 回顾了微软在早期试图主导和控制技术标准的策略，提到微软曾试图阻碍开源技术的发展，并分享了自己在企业环境中支持Mozilla Firefox而非IE的经历。
• [disruptiveink] 质疑TLS 1.0是否仅仅是对SSL 3.0的轻微修改，认为文章低估了两者之间的差异。
• [webprofusion] 认为在实际操作中，大多数人只关心HTTPS能否正常工作，而不太关注其内部机制，因此对TLS和SSL的区分并不重要。
• [aramattamara] 提出是否可以把下一版本的协议重新命名为SSL，因为SSL仍然被广泛使用。
• [achillean] 提供了数据显示仍有超过30万互联网服务支持SSLv2，并指出尽管数量在减少，但SSLv2仍会存在一段时间。
• [tptacek] 强调在2014年时，SSL 2.0被明确认为有严重缺陷，特别是其握手过程未经过适当的身份验证。
• [yardstick] 提出如果TLS版本从TLS 3.0开始，是否会更容易被接受，以便与SSL版本对应。
• [chollida1] 提到微软和Netscape在SSL/TLS标准化过程中的竞争，认为Netscape在某些情况下表现得不够合作，而微软则提供了更好的实现方案。

补充讨论：
• [amenghra] 推荐了Eric Rescorla的书《SSL and TLS: Designing and Building Secure Systems》作为理解TLS历史和问题的有用资源。
• [WhyNotHugo] 赞赏文章的写作风格，认为其信息丰富且具有个性。

争议焦点：
• SSL和TLS版本之间的实际差异程度，特别是TLS 1.0是否只是对SSL 3.0的轻微修改。
• 在实际应用中，是否需要对TLS和SSL进行明确区分。
• 微软和Netscape在早期浏览器大战中的角色和影响。

Tim Dierks
May 23, 2014
Security Standards and Name Changes in the Browser Wars
The Netscape/Microsoft browser wars in the mid-90's were really vicious and competitive. They really had it out for each other.
Netscape had developed the SSL protocol. The initial version had cryptographic flaws and was broken pretty quickly, and never released. The first production version was SSL 2, which was in use for a few years. (I don't know the exact versions of Navigator it shipped in.)
SSL 2 had some flaws, both cryptographic and practical; not dramatic enough to make replacing it a crisis, but it clearly needed some work from early on.
As a part of the cutthroat competition, Microsoft decided to revise the SSL 2 protocol with some additions of their own, and specified a protocol called "PCT" that was derived from SSL 2. It was only supported in IE and IIS.
Netscape also wanted to address SSL 2 issues, but wasn't going to let Microsoft take leadership/ownership in the standard, so they developed SSL 3.0, which was a more significant departure.
Various people in the industry & community didn't want a fork, so we (Consensus Development, where I worked with
Christopher Allen
at the time, and where I had written the
SSL 3.0 reference implementation
under contract to Netscape) hosted a meeting between representatives from Netscape and Microsoft; I forget everyone who was there, but I recall that
Bruce Schneier
was there (before he was famous), and probably
Paul Kocher
, who had designed the SSL 3 protocol; Barbara Fox represented Microsoft. And we negotiated a deal where Microsoft and Netscape would both support the IETF taking over the protocol and standardizing it in an open process, which led to me editing the RFC.
As a part of the horsetrading, we had to make some changes to SSL 3.0 (so it wouldn't look the IETF was just rubberstamping Netscape's protocol), and we had to rename the protocol (for the same reason). And thus was born TLS 1.0 (which was really SSL 3.1). And of course, now, in retrospect, the whole thing looks silly.

44282378.article_summary: 这篇文章回顾了90年代中期Netscape与微软在浏览器大战期间的竞争，特别是在安全协议SSL上的较量。Netscape最初开发了SSL协议，但SSL 2.0存在缺陷。微软为了竞争推出了基于SSL 2.0的PCT协议。Netscape则开发了SSL 3.0以解决这些问题，但行业内希望避免协议分裂。经过协商，双方同意让IETF标准化该协议，导致SSL 3.0被修改并重命名为TLS 1.0（实质上是SSL 3.1），从而避免了专有标准的竞争。
44282378.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SSL/TLS协议的发展、区别及其历史背景

不同观点：
• [ekr____] 指出SSL和TLS的不同版本之间存在显著差异，特别是SSLv2、SSLv3、TLS 1.0、TLS 1.1和TLS 1.2的演变过程，强调每个版本在设计时都考虑了自动协商版本的机制，以确保客户端和服务器可以独立升级而不影响连接。
• [Timothycquinn] 回顾了微软在早期试图主导和控制技术标准的策略，提到微软曾试图阻碍开源技术的发展，并分享了自己在企业环境中支持Mozilla Firefox而非IE的经历。
• [disruptiveink] 质疑TLS 1.0是否仅仅是对SSL 3.0的轻微修改，认为文章低估了两者之间的差异。
• [webprofusion] 认为在实际操作中，大多数人只关心HTTPS能否正常工作，而不太关注其内部机制，因此对TLS和SSL的区分并不重要。
• [aramattamara] 提出是否可以把下一版本的协议重新命名为SSL，因为SSL仍然被广泛使用。
• [achillean] 提供了数据显示仍有超过30万互联网服务支持SSLv2，并指出尽管数量在减少，但SSLv2仍会存在一段时间。
• [tptacek] 强调在2014年时，SSL 2.0被明确认为有严重缺陷，特别是其握手过程未经过适当的身份验证。
• [yardstick] 提出如果TLS版本从TLS 3.0开始，是否会更容易被接受，以便与SSL版本对应。
• [chollida1] 提到微软和Netscape在SSL/TLS标准化过程中的竞争，认为Netscape在某些情况下表现得不够合作，而微软则提供了更好的实现方案。

补充讨论：
• [amenghra] 推荐了Eric Rescorla的书《SSL and TLS: Designing and Building Secure Systems》作为理解TLS历史和问题的有用资源。
• [WhyNotHugo] 赞赏文章的写作风格，认为其信息丰富且具有个性。

争议焦点：
• SSL和TLS版本之间的实际差异程度，特别是TLS 1.0是否只是对SSL 3.0的轻微修改。
• 在实际应用中，是否需要对TLS和SSL进行明确区分。
• 微软和Netscape在早期浏览器大战中的角色和影响。

data.title: McKinsey Leans on AI to Make PowerPoints, Draft Proposals
data.author: JumpCrisscross
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在商业简报和幻灯片制作中的应用及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **xt00** 认为AI总结简报是合理的，因为接收简报的人也会使用AI来总结内容。这暗示AI在简报处理中的双重应用，提高了效率。

• **afavour** 以讽刺的语气预测2025年“最符合品牌特色的揭露”将获奖，暗示对AI生成内容的品牌一致性或创新性的质疑。

• **aussiegreenie** 对高价AI幻灯片 deck 表示嘲讽，称之为“百万美元AI幻灯片”，并强调其平庸性（“NOW WITH MORE BANALITY”），质疑其性价比。

• **smartbit** 提供了一个存档链接，但没有发表具体观点，可能是为讨论提供参考资料。

• **fshafique** 关注分析师的具体工作任务和时间/资金分配，询问数据收集、分析、预测以及制作PowerPoint的比例，并提到麦肯锡幻灯片的信息密度，希望了解AI生成内容的实际效果。

• **cosmicgadget** 认为现有的公式化幻灯片已经不够好，而AI生成的公式化幻灯片可能会更糟，但只要符合基本的格式要求（如最小字体大小），也可以接受。

• **darth_avocado** 直言不讳地指出高价商业简报本质上是编造的“ nonsense ”，并认为让ChatGPT来编造比刚毕业的“高级顾问”更可取，反映出对传统咨询行业的不满和对AI的更高期望。

补充讨论：
- 评论中对AI生成内容的质量和性价比存在争议，特别是其能否真正提升效率和内容质量。
- 讨论还涉及AI在商业简报中应用的实际效果，包括与传统人工制作的对比。
- 对AI生成幻灯片的公式化和信息密度问题也有一定关注。

data.title: Studio Ghibli marks 40 years, but future looks uncertain
data.author: gslin
data.article_summary: Studio Ghibli庆祝成立40周年，凭借复杂剧情和精美手绘动画赢得全球影迷喜爱，曾两次获得奥斯卡奖。然而，其未来充满不确定性，尤其在84岁高龄的联合创始人宫崎骏可能推出最后一部作品《男孩与隼》后。随着2024年再次荣获奥斯卡，以及Netflix全球流媒体播放，Ghibli的影响力持续增长。同时，人工智能生成图像引发的版权问题也引发关注。在信息过载和误导泛滥的时代，优质新闻报道显得尤为重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Studio Ghibli是否应随着宫崎骏的退休而结束

不同观点：
• coldtea和部分其他用户认为Studio Ghibli的核心是宫崎骏，他的退休或离世意味着Studio Ghibli的精神和艺术灵魂将随之消逝。他们强调宫崎骏对工作室的不可替代性。
• astnai和IG_Semmelweiss等人则持相反观点，认为伟大的工作室可以超越其创始人的存在，通过新的人才延续其精神和愿景。他们以苹果公司为例，说明即使创始人离去，公司仍能继续运作并传承其遗产。
• StopDisinfo910指出Studio Ghibli是一个为高畑勋和宫崎骏设立的制作平台，虽然宫崎骏是灵魂人物，但工作室本身是一个中型公司，拥有众多员工和项目，可以继续运作，即使可能无法再制作出同样高水准的电影。
• HideousKojima认为，虽然高畑勋和宫崎骏是工作室的核心，但宫崎吾朗等新一代导演尚未展现出同样的才华和远见。他们对《雀斑少爷》感到失望，并认为即使工作室继续存在，也难以再现过去的辉煌。

补充讨论：
• rvz对当前Studio Ghibli的状况持悲观态度，认为其风格已被破坏，不再有过去的魅力。
• kilimounjaro提到Studio Ghibli的形象生成在AI领域有巨大影响，甚至与OpenAI的成长有关，建议Studio Ghibli应获得相应的经济回报。
• godzillabrennus分享了个人对Studio Ghibli作品的喜爱，并希望下一代工作室能够继续探索宫崎骏所创造的宇宙，同时表达了对AI技术在这一领域应用的期待。

争议焦点：
• Studio Ghibli是否应随着宫崎骏的退休而结束，核心争议在于宫崎骏个人对工作室的不可替代性以及新一代人才是否能延续其精神和艺术水准。

Studio Ghibli marks 40 years, but future looks uncertain
Vice president of events and exhibitions for Studio Ghibli, Kenichi Yoda (right), and director and Ghibli Park creative development manager, Goro Miyazaki (left), pose at the 77th edition of the Cannes Film Festival before receiving an Honorary Palme d'Or.

Jun 6, 2025
Japan's Studio Ghibli turns 40 this month with two Oscars and legions of fans young and old won over by its complex plots and fantastical hand-drawn animation.
But the future is uncertain, with latest hit
"The Boy and the Heron"
likely — but not certainly — the final feature from celebrated co-founder Hayao Miyazaki, now 84. In March, the
internet was flooded with pictures
in Studio Ghibli's distinctively nostalgic style after the release of OpenAI's newest image generator — raising questions over copyright.
The studio behind the Oscar-winning "Spirited Away" has become a cultural phenomenon since Miyazaki and the late Isao Takahata — he passed away in 2018 — established it in 1985. Its popularity has been fueled of late by a second Academy Award in 2024 for "The Boy and the Heron," starring Robert Pattinson, and by Netflix streaming Ghibli movies around the world.
